pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
Ohm Sweet Ohm

A logic puzzle in twenty-three circuit boards

In 1994 the Bitmore family of Juniper Lane had the first Smart Home on the block. Every appliance in the house talked to every other appliance: the coffee maker woke the toaster, the toaster warmed up the TV, and the TV told the garage door when the news was over.

Then came the thunderstorm. One bolt of lightning hit the TV antenna, ran down the house wiring and scrambled everything. Now the toaster opens the garage door. The fridge changes the channel. The clock radio plays polka at three in the morning.

Somebody has to fix it. Somebody small.

Watt is a pocket-sized repair robot who lives in the main fuse box, right next to his charging socket. The lightning bounced him clear across the house and into the toaster! To get home, Watt must roll through the circuit board of every haywire appliance - in the kitchen, the living room, the garage and the attic - rewiring as he goes.

Live current will fizzle a little robot in a blink. But current is also the only thing that switches off the force-field gates between Watt and home. Flip the switches, follow the copper, and think before you roll.

There's no place like Ohm!

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type OHMSWEET and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the clack of the switches; without one, the PC speaker beeps along.

A short cartoon shows the storm. Press any key for the menu and pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Watt will show you how the first board is done.

Before each board a card shows its name and a picture of it. Press any key (or wait a moment) and Watt drops onto the GND pad in the middle of the board. Somewhere on the board is an outlet: roll onto it and you are through to the next board.

Spare batteries

Watt starts with 20 spare batteries (the F2 screen counts them). Every time he touches live current, or you reboot the board, he uses one up and the board starts over, exactly as it was. Each outlet you reach gives you one more, and so does each gold screw. Run out and the game is over.

Press F5 to save your game between tries and F6 to load it.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Controls

KeyWhat it does
Up W 8Roll up one block
Down S 2Roll down one block
Left A 4Roll left one block
Right D 6Roll right one block
RReboot: start this board over (costs a spare battery)
F1Help
F2Score and spare batteries
F3 / F4Music / sound effects on and off
F5 / F6Save / load a game
EscQuit to the menu

Watt rolls exactly one block for each press of a key, so he is always squarely on the board. There are no diagonal moves: circuit boards are wired in straight lines, and so is Watt.

To work a switch, a timer button or a fuse, just roll into it. You bump it and stay where you are.

pages.head: Current
pages.html:
Current

Batteries sit in the housing at the edge of a board, each one feeding its own copper wire. A steady stream of glowing beads runs out along the wire: that is live current. Touch a bead and Watt fizzles.

Current is not instant. When a switch is turned on, you can watch the current race down the wire, about as fast as Watt can roll. When it is turned off, the last beads still have to run out to the end before the wire is safe.

A wire with no beads on it is dead and perfectly safe to roll over.

Force-field gates

The crackling yellow gates stand between Watt and the outlet. A gate is deadly to touch. But a gate is always at the end of a wire, and the moment current reaches it, the gate shuts down for good. After that its posts soak up any current that follows, so the doorway is safe.

That is the heart of every board: get current to the gates without getting current on Watt.

Kinds of battery

  • Green batteries run steadily, all the time.
  • Pulsing batteries (marked ~) blink on and off, sending current down the wire in bursts with gaps between. Two pulsing batteries often take turns.
  • Dead batteries (marked !) do nothing until Watt bumps them. Then they start, and they never, ever stop.

pages.head: Parts
pages.html:
Parts on the Board

PartWhat it does
Knife switchBump it to flip it. Down (on) lets current through; up (off) stops it. Flip it as often as you like.
Timer buttonBump it and it lets current through for about five seconds, then turns itself off. Watch the clock hand go round.
FuseCarries current until Watt bumps it. Then it blows and its wire is dead forever.
Diode (arrow)Watt can roll through it only the way the arrow points. Once past, there is no going back!
Relay NONormally open. Ordinary current can't get through until pink control current reaches the relay. Then it is thrown, and stays thrown.
Relay NCNormally closed. Ordinary current runs straight through until pink control current reaches it. Then it opens, and stays open.
555 timerA little eight-legged chip that pulses its wire, on a little longer than off (wired the usual way, a 555 is always on longer than off). Its red OUT light goes dark with the current.
LCD screen, CitiCarCurrent lights them up, then runs on through to whatever is next. A blank LCD shows a row of boxes; booted, it says READY.
OutletThe way out. 1,000 points and a spare battery.
Gold screw500 points and a spare battery.

Reading the wires

Copper traces show where every wire goes, even when it is dead, so you can always follow a wire from its battery to its gate. Where two wires cross, one hops over the other on a little bridge: they are not connected. Where a wire runs through the housing it can't hurt Watt, and Watt can't reach the parts there.

Pink control current is ordinary current's bossy big sister: it throws relays, and ordinary current can't cross it.

pages.head: Thinking Like an Electrician
pages.html:
Thinking Like an Electrician

Every board can be solved, and none needs fast fingers: a little patience and a little planning will do. Some tips from the Sandbox Software testing bench:

  • Follow every wire from its battery to its end before you touch anything. Ask: when this is live, where can't I go?
  • Gates remember. Once a gate has had current, it's open for good. You can turn the power off again afterwards, and you usually should.
  • Switches in a row all have to be on for current to get past. Current gets as far as the first switch that is off, so the wire before it is live.
  • Two wires into one gate means either one will do. Pick the one that won't fence you in.
  • One-way trips (diodes, dead batteries, fuses, relays) can't be undone. Do them last, or do them in the right order.
  • Watch the beads. Pulsing current comes in bursts: wait right next to the wire, and roll across just after a burst goes by. You roll exactly as fast as current runs, so you can even ride along right behind a burst.
  • Stuck? Press R to reboot the board. It costs one spare battery, and every board starts exactly as it was.

news.head: Ohm Sweet Ohm: puzzles made of pure Game-Maker
news.html: A thunderstorm has scrambled the Bitmores' brand-new Smart Home, and Watt, the pocket-sized repair robot who lives in the fuse box, must roll home through twenty-three haywire circuit boards, from the toaster to the attic. Every switch, fuse and relay is built from ordinary Game-Maker blocks and monsters: batteries are blocks that give birth to "current" monsters, and gates fall when a stronger monster touches them. Not one line of code!

news.head: Since last issue: A year of Sparky mail
news.html: It has been a while since issue 2, and the mailbag filled up. Your favorite gadget in In The Year 2000! was the Teleport-A-Phone. Your least favorite moment was running out of quarters at the Phone Exchange (every room has more, and they come back each time you dial). Three of you sent drawings of Sparky 3000, and one of you built him out of a shoebox and two flashlights.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: New address, new computer
news.html: Where did we go? The founder finished high school, a 486 with a CD-ROM drive turned up as a graduation present, and Sandbox Software moved to Pittsburgh, where the founder is studying at the Art Institute of Pittsburgh. You can see it on the boxes. The best part of the new desk is a modem: our own BBS is online at 1-412-555-SAND, and every Sandbox game, hint and high-score list goes there first.

news.head: In the workshop: Can Game-Maker scroll a shooter?
news.html: Everybody on the BBS says Game-Maker can't do a real scrolling shoot-'em-up. We think it can. The workbench has a nano-fighter, a lot of graph paper covered in circuit traces, and a title: Virus Blaster. A hint: it's set somewhere very close to you right now.

news.head: Letters: "Is the pocket telephone real?"
news.html:
"Dex's science report is about a telephone that fits in your pocket. Is that a real invention?" - A reader, by mail

The Scoop replies: Not yet. In our BBS poll it got two votes, and one of those was a joke. Ask us again in the year 2000.

items.title: Ohm Sweet Ohm Hint Book
items.note: A nudge and an answer for every board
items.intro: Stuck on a board? Find it below. The question tells you what most people get stuck on; the answer, printed under red, tells you how to get past. Read the answers through the red film, one at a time, and only when you need them! (Heard the felt-maker left something behind in the wiring? See the last page.)

hints.q: The Toaster: How do I get past the crackling gate?
hints.a: Bump the switch from below to turn it on. Current runs along the wire to the gate and shuts it down. Keep off the wire while it glows!

hints.q: The Blender: The gate is open, but the wire next to it is live!
hints.a: A gate stays open once current has reached it. Bump the switch again to turn the power off, wait for the last spark to drain away, then walk through.

hints.q: The Microwave: Two switches and one gate. Which one?
hints.a: Either switch opens the gate: two wires into one gate means either will do. The left switch puts live current right in front of the gate (turn it off again if you use it). The right one keeps its current inside the housing.

hints.q: The Dishwasher: The second switch fences me away from the second gate!
hints.a: Two gates, one after the other. Open the first with the switch at the top left. For the second, slip around behind its switch BEFORE you turn it on, and bump it from below: then the live wire is behind you.

hints.q: The Fridge: I rolled through the arrow and now I cannot get back to the switch.
hints.a: The arrow is a diode: you can only go through it the way it points. Before you go through, turn the switch on, wait for the gate to open, and turn the switch OFF again.

hints.q: The Coffee Maker: I turned the top switch on and now I am stuck down by the bottom switch!
hints.a: Two switches in a row both have to be on. Turn on the bottom one FIRST, while the wire is still dead, then the top one. When the gate opens, turn the top switch off again so you can step over the wire.

hints.q: The Doorbell: The button turns the current on, and then I am fenced out.
hints.a: It is a timer button: it turns the current off again by itself after a few seconds. Push it, watch the gate shut down, wait for the wire to go dark, then walk in. (Or push it from the inside!)

hints.q: The TV Set: If I turn the power on, I can never cross that wire. If I don't, the gate stays shut.
hints.a: That is a timer button, not a switch. Bump it as you go by: it turns itself off after about five seconds. Wait for the gate to open and the wire to go dark, then cross.

hints.q: The VCR: The current keeps coming and going. How do I get across?
hints.a: Those batteries pulse: on for a moment, off for a moment, and the two take turns. Wait next to a wire until the current has just gone by, then roll across. Stop between the two wires and do it again.

hints.q: The Floor Lamp: One wire is always live, and there is no switch for it!
hints.a: Bump a fuse and it blows for good, and its wire goes dead. Follow the copper: the LEFT fuse feeds the wire in front of the gate. Blow that one, never the right one (it feeds the gate). Then turn on the switch.

hints.q: The Stereo: I bumped the battery with the red "!" and now I am stuck.
hints.a: A dead battery starts when you bump it, and it never stops. That one feeds the wire in front of the gate. Use the switch at the top instead: its wire stays inside the housing.

hints.q: The Night-Light: The corridor is wired end to end, and the current never stops!
hints.a: It does stop, for a moment: a 555 is high a little longer than it is low. Watch the red LED. When it goes out, the last spark races off down the wire: roll in right behind it and keep rolling. Duck into a nook to wait for the next one.

hints.q: The Garage Door Opener: The battery will not stop, and its wire is in my way.
hints.a: Start the battery, and wait for the gate to open. Then bump the fuse next to the battery: it blows and the wire goes dead for good. Blow it too early and the gate never opens.

hints.q: The Wet-Dry Vac: Once I roll over the arrow I can never get back to the battery.
hints.a: Start the battery first, then roll over the arrow. The fuse is on the far side: blow it once the gate has opened, and the wire in front of the gate goes dead.

hints.q: The Power Drill: The red wire runs into a box marked NO. What is that?
hints.a: It is a relay, Normally Open: red current can not get through until pink control current hits it. Then it stays thrown. Turn on the switch on the pink wire, wait, then head for the gate.

hints.q: The Lawn Mower: Once I am past the arrows I can not turn the red wire off again.
hints.a: The box marked NC is a relay, Normally Closed: red current runs through it until pink control current hits it, then it opens for good. Turn the red switch on as you roll by (you will not get another chance), then use the pink switch to cut the red wire in front of the gate.

hints.q: The Christmas Lights: Every switch has to be on at once, but then I am fenced in!
hints.a: Switches in a row: current gets as far as the first one that is off. Work so the live wire never fences you in: turn the switch just above you OFF first, cross over and turn the top one on, come back, turn the middle one on again, then the bottom one. When the gate opens, turn the bottom one off and walk around.

hints.q: The CitiCar: I plugged it in and the headlights came on. Now the charging cord is in my way!
hints.a: A charger will not send a single volt until the car answers on the pink pilot wire, and then it does not stop until the car is full. Turn on the pilot, wait for the headlights, then roll around below the charger and pop its breaker (the fuse).

hints.q: The Home Computer: Both pink switches open the gate. Why do I keep getting stuck?
hints.a: Trace the wires through the chip. The left switch lets the TOP red wire through, and that one ends up running right in front of the gate, for good. The right switch lets the BOTTOM red wire through, inside the housing. Use only the right switch (and never both: each one shuts the other path).

hints.q: The Clock Radio: Snooze button, flashing wires, one-way arrows... where do I start?
hints.a: Bump the timer button as you roll over the arrows. It lets the pulses through for a few seconds, long enough to open the gate. Then wait for it to go off, cross, and slip through the flashing wire between pulses.

hints.q: The Electric Train: Two gates, a switch, a dead battery and a fuse. Where do I start?
hints.a: One gate at a time. Switch on the top wire from above, wait for the left gate, switch it off and go through. Then start the dead battery from below, blow its fuse as soon as the top gate has opened, and walk around to the gate.

hints.q: The Breadboard Computer: The clock never stops racing up the hall, and the screen is just a row of boxes.
hints.a: Run it like the real thing: HALT, then STEP. The pink switch at the bottom throws the relay that halts the 555 clock. Then bump the STEP button: one tick of current boots the LCD (READY!) and opens the gate. The hall is dark now.

hints.q: Home Sweet Ohm: I pressed the timer button, but nothing happened!
hints.a: The timer only lets current through if it is already waiting there. First slip across the flashing wire and turn on the switch in the bottom wall, come back, THEN roll over the arrows and press the timer. Wait for the gate, wait for the wire to go dark, and go home.

hints.q: Some say the felt-maker left something behind in the wiring. Where?
hints.a: In the garage. One board's housing isn't quite as solid as it looks.

hints.q: Which board?
hints.a: The Garage Door Opener (board 13). Look along the bottom of its housing for the faint outline of a little access panel.

hints.q: Show me the wiring.
hints.a: On The Garage Door Opener, roll down from the pad, left along the bottom row to the corner, and keep rolling down into the seam. You land in the house's main fuse box. Roll onto the felt egg and press the space bar to pick it up, then roll into the black main switch to get back.

pages.head: The Light Went Out
pages.html:
Maximus: The Hundred Worlds

Sector Zero, the year the stars went quiet.

For ten thousand years the Maximus Core burned at the heart of the galaxy: a forge-star whose light ran down the warp lanes to every inhabited world. Couriers rode that light from planet to planet, carrying everything from seed grain to love letters.

Then the Core cracked. Its light was held in ten star-shards, and when it broke they were flung across the Hundred Worlds. The warp lanes are failing. Sector by sector, the galaxy is going quiet.

Max is a courier at Maxima Station. Couriers deliver. This time the package is the light of the galaxy: find the ten shards, carry them through the gates, fly the Maelstrom, and bring them home to the Heart.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Installing

Copy every file on the disk into one directory, for example C:\MAXIMUS, and type MAXIMUS. You need a 386 or better with VGA and 640K. A Sound Blaster plays the music and the digitized effects; without one, the PC speaker plays them.

The menu

  • Play starts at Maxima Station's training deck.
  • Read Instructions, Read Storyline and See Credits show the pages from this manual on screen.
  • Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Max shows you around the training deck himself.

The training deck

The deck teaches as you go: walk, hop the crates, pick up credits, shoot the practice drones, pay the credit door, ride the lift and walk into the airlock. Then you are in the pod.

One thing stands between the lift and the airlock: the clearance gate. Climb the ledge to the clerk's window and step into it for your departure form, which stamps a dock, a world and a courier badge. Set the dock, the world and the badge on the Courier's Star Wheel from the box, read its two windows in order, and press the one hatch of the three that wears the same two pictures. The wrong hatches only sigh and send you back, so a courier without the wheel can simply try them in turn.

Lives and saving

You start with 3 lives and 100 hit points. Lose them all and the signal is lost. Save often with F5: it is a big galaxy.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Keys

Left RightWalk, swim, drive or thrust
UpJet hop on foot (tap again in the air to climb), thrust in the pod and the bell, jump with Spring Shocks in the rover
DownCurl into a ball (on foot), dive, brake
SpaceFire, in the direction you last moved
G / BPick up / drop a module
THail (say hello)
F1Help
F2Status: score, credits, hit points, lives and your modules
F3 / F4Music / sound on and off
F5 / F6Save / load
EscQuit

The number pad's 8 4 6 2 work the same as the arrows. W/A/S/D are not a second set of arrows here: W fires the Flak Cannon. Pick up with G and drop with B, under the left hand while the right steers and away from W/A/S/D, so a WASD habit can't throw a module away.

Module keys

ZPlasma Lance
XNova Core
Q / EDash Boots
CShield Emitter
FHover Pack
VMine Layer
RMed Kit
WFlak Cannon
Q / E (sub)Hydro Jets
Up (rover)Spring Shocks

pages.head: Four Ways to Travel
pages.html:
The courier pod

Space charts are flown in the pod. The arrows fire its thrusters; let go and it brakes. Fly into the middle of a planet to land, into a warp ring to jump.

On foot

Max's suit has grav-jets: Up is a hop, and another tap in the air hops again. Hold Right while you tap Up to sail over gaps. Walk into the uplink beacon behind you to return to orbit.

The diving bell

On sea worlds Max takes the bell. It swims at a steady pace with the arrows and holds still when you let go. Bubble columns lift you, currents push you. Surface at the buoy to leave.

The rover

Rover worlds are fast and flat. The rover rides the lifts at every step; with the Spring Shocks module it can jump.

pages.head: The Galaxy and the Shards
pages.html:
Sector gates

The galaxy chart holds five sector warps around the dead Core. The Cradle is open; every other sector is sealed by crystal gates, two to a sector. A gate opens when you touch it carrying its shard, and the shards stay with you for good.

SectorGate needsWorlds
1. The Cradleopen18
2. EmberreachRuby + Amber18
3. The ShallowsCitrine + Emerald18
4. GlasswindJade + Aqua18
5. The Deep BlackSapphire + Amethyst16
The Coreall ten3

Jump rings

Every sector chart also holds a jump ring, walled in behind the next sector's crystal gates: carry those shards and it takes you straight on. The ring in The Deep Black leads to the Maelstrom itself.

Finding shards

Planets with a gold signal beside them on the sector chart hold a shard, deep in a vault. The planet card you see on landing says where you are (SECTOR 2 OF 5, WORLD 9 OF 18), names the shard and which of the ten it is (SHARD 3 OF 10), reminds you that F5 saves, and its long-range scan shows the whole world: where you land (green) and where the vault lies (gold).

The Core

All ten shards open the way to the Core. Fly the Maelstrom, a storm canyon so packed with rock that your weapons jam, to the Citadel, whose vault holds the teleporter to the Heart. There the Guardian's armor plates stand across the hall, and down their middle runs a seal of light that opens only to the Core's own spark. The Heart Eye circles in front of it and swoops when you come near. Crack it three times, with a plasma bolt, a shield orb or by ramming it (that hurts), and it bursts into the Core Light, which finds you and charges the seal: then walk through. Plasma cracks the plates; shouldering into them works too, for a few hit points.

Trading posts

Each chart has a trading post. Nudge a pad to buy: an extra life (100 credits), repairs (20), plasma cells (30), nova charges (40), shield charges (30) and med kits (50). One of each per visit.

pages.head: Worlds and Vaults
pages.html:
What you will find

  • Credits (green chips), gems (score), hearts (hit points), 1-Ups and ammo cells for your modules.
  • Vaults deep underground hold the shards and modules. A credit door costs 10 credits to open; a force field blinks on and off.
  • Crystal walls shatter at a touch, and some rock is not rock at all: secret pockets hide treasure.
  • Lifts and bubble columns carry you up; winds and currents push you along.
  • Lava, acid and brine hurt, but the jolt hops you out. A healing spring in the caves mends 100 hit points in one long drink, then runs dry until you land on that world again.
  • Nests in cave walls send out creatures until you leave.

pages.head: Courier Modules
pages.html:
The ten modules

Modules lie in planet vaults. Press G to pick one up; it stays in your inventory (F2) and works in every vehicle that can use it.

ModuleKeyWhere
Plasma LanceZLittle Hollow, The Cradle
Nova CoreXPyre, Emberreach
Dash BootsQ / ECopperfield, The Cradle
Shield EmitterCMistral Isle, The Shallows
Hover PackFScorchmark, Emberreach
Mine LayerVRimefall, Glasswind
Med KitROutpost Nine, The Cradle
Flak CannonWVenom Marsh, Glasswind
Hydro JetsQ / E (sub)Tidewater, The Shallows
Spring ShocksUp (rover)Redrock, Emberreach

Ammunition counts carry from vehicle to vehicle. The Plasma Lance is the only weapon that cracks armor; the Shield Emitter's guard orb stops almost anything.

pages.head: Creatures
pages.html:
On the worlds

GloopA hopping slime. Harmless alone, never alone.
Gloop MotherSplits into a Gloopling when shot.
GlooplingSmall, fast, and it follows you.
ShellbackA beetle walking its beat.
IronbackArmored. Blaster bolts bounce off; use the Plasma Lance.
DropwebHangs from cave ceilings and drops on you.
FlitterA cave bat with no sense of direction.
ScreechA bigger bat that dives when you come near.
StingerWasps home in on courier suits.

In the seas

MinnowSmall fry darting about in schools.
SnapfinA toothy little fish that comes straight for you.
BigfinCruises back and forth along the reef.
AnglerWaits in the dark, then lunges at your lamp.
Ribbon EelSwims long laps through open water.
MorayLurks in holes and snaps at passers-by.

In space

Void JellyDrifts between the stars.
Void MiteTiny, fast and drawn to engines.
Pirate SkiffFlies a patrol line.
Pirate AceHunts couriers for their cargo.
RaiderFlies figure eights around its loot.
Scout DroneWanders and watches.

On the stations

CrawlerA maintenance bot gone bad.
Sentry DroneWanders the corridors.
Gun TurretBolted to the deck. Armored.
Security BotArmored patroller.
Spider BotDrops from the ceiling.
Hover MineBobs in place.

Star whales are gentle and swim in pods. Every whale in a pod follows the same loop at the same moment, so a pod keeps its shape: look for thirteen of them circling on the galaxy chart, and for a pod in The Cradle that spells somebody's name.

Most creatures burst when they hit you. A few things - flytraps, magma, tumbling asteroids, the Phantom - cannot be hurt at all: keep moving.

pages.head: Registering Maximus
pages.html:
This is shareware

Copy it, share it, upload it. If you enjoy Maximus, please register: registration is $15 and gets you the printed manual with a fold-out galaxy chart, the courier's sector map of all 88 worlds and their vaults, the hint book, and news of our next game.

Send a check or money order (US funds) to:

Sandbox Software
Attn: Maximus Registration
P.O. Box 000
Pittsburgh, PA 15213

Credits

Designed and built by Claude for Sandbox Software, with Game-Maker 2.0 by Recreational Software Designs. Every world, sprite, song and sound was made by a program from a seed.

Hails

Three worlds call you before you land. Galileo is an old Earth probe still running a loop on its RCA 1802 (the real chip flew to Jupiter). Liberty keeps a cracked bell under thirteen stars, and an archive of every letter a courier ever brought. On Boxcar Flats, Doc Leo, PhD (Comedic Science), will walk your parcel over with his rubber chicken. Answer them all!

Dedicated to three real couriers: Lewis's mother, a letter carrier; his father, who kept the post office running in maintenance; and his grandmother, a postal clerk. All three were at the post office when he bought Game-Maker in 1992.

pages.head: Pushing the Limits
pages.html:
How far Game-Maker goes

Maximus was built to stand on every edge of Game-Maker 2.0. These are the limits we found in its file formats and in PLAYGAME, and how much of each this game uses (also in LIMITS.TXT on the disk).

LimitMaximumMaximus uses
Scenes in a .GAM231 (PLAYGAME allocates all scenes in one 64K block of 283-byte records)100: title, ending, training deck, galaxy, 5 sectors, 88 worlds, Maelstrom, Citadel, Heart, with four one-page scenes besides (Between Worlds and the three pages of the clearance gate). We stopped at 100: 28300 bytes of scene records sit easily in DOS memory, every scene still loads in a moment, and the integrator's 310x165 world view still shows each scene box and link
Scene file-name pool65,520 bytes (PLAYGAME clamps it at 0xFFF0)3004 bytes

Inventory slots1010 courier modules

printables.pitch: Courier Max flies, walks, drives and dives across 88 worlds to bring ten star-shards home and relight the dead star at the heart of the galaxy.

items.heading: THE HUNDRED WORLDS

The Core: the Maelstrom, the Citadel, the Heart.

items.title: Courier’s sector map
items.heading: COURIER’S SECTOR MAP: ALL 88 WORLDS
items.intro: Every world in the five sectors, how you get around on it, and what its vault holds. Gold signal worlds hold a shard; module vaults hold courier gear.

items.title: The Courier's Star Wheel
items.note: Three discs: a dock, a world and a courier badge give a two-picture clearance code
items.heading: THE COURIER'S STAR WHEEL · Maxima Station clearance codes
howto: Every departure form on Maxima Station carries three stamps: a dock letter, a world of origin and a courier badge.
Turn the big disc until the form's dock letter is under the arrow, the middle disc until its world is, and the small disc until its badge is.

The small disc has two windows. Read them in order, FIRST then SECOND: each shows a picture. Over a printed spot on the middle disc a window shows that picture; over a hole it looks through to the big disc. Press the hatch in the pod bay that wears the same two pictures, top to bottom.

puzzles.ask: Maxima Station's pod bay: the clerk's form says dock F, world Prism, badge Chevron. Which of the three hatches opens?
puzzles.answer: The heart, then the bolt: the middle hatch, the one between the rocket pair and the heart-and-key. The others only sigh.

items.title: Maximus Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Find your question, then slide the red film over the answer under it. Read one answer at a time: a courier who knows everything has nothing left to find.

hints.q: How do I get off the training deck?
hints.a: Pay the credit door with the credits you pick up, ride the lift, and get through the clearance gate in the pod bay (see the next question). Then walk into the airlock. The pod is waiting.

hints.q: Which of the three hatches in the pod bay opens?
hints.a: Climb the ledge to the clerk's window and step into it: the form shows your dock, world and badge. Turn the Courier's Star Wheel from the box to that world and badge and read its CODE window; the hatch wearing that picture is the one. No wheel? It is the middle one. The others only sigh and send you back, and nothing is lost.

hints.q: How do I land on a planet?
hints.a: Fly the pod into the middle of the planet on the sector chart.

hints.q: How do I get back to space?
hints.a: Walk into the uplink beacon behind you where you landed. On sea worlds, surface at the buoy.

hints.q: I keep running out of lives.
hints.a: Buy an extra life at the trading post for 100 credits, and save with F5 before every vault.

hints.q: Where is the Ruby shard?
hints.a: Ambermoor, in The Cradle. Look for the gold signal on the sector chart, then use the long-range scan on the planet card to find the vault.

hints.q: Where is the Amber shard?
hints.a: Brightwater, in The Cradle. Look for the gold signal on the sector chart, then use the long-range scan on the planet card to find the vault.

hints.q: Where do I find the Plasma Lance?
hints.a: In a vault on Little Hollow, in The Cradle. Press G to pick it up; its key is Z.

hints.q: Where do I find the Nova Core?
hints.a: In a vault on Pyre, in Emberreach. Press G to pick it up; its key is X.

hints.q: Where do I find the Dash Boots?
hints.a: In a vault on Copperfield, in The Cradle. Press G to pick it up; its key is Q / E.

hints.q: Where do I find the Shield Emitter?
hints.a: In a vault on Mistral Isle, in The Shallows. Press G to pick it up; its key is C.

hints.q: Where do I find the Hover Pack?
hints.a: In a vault on Scorchmark, in Emberreach. Press G to pick it up; its key is F.

hints.q: Where do I find the Mine Layer?
hints.a: In a vault on Rimefall, in Glasswind. Press G to pick it up; its key is V.

hints.q: Where do I find the Flak Cannon?
hints.a: In a vault on Venom Marsh, in Glasswind. Press G to pick it up; its key is W.

hints.q: My blaster bounces off a creature.
hints.a: It is armored, like an Ironback or a Gun Turret. Only the Plasma Lance (Z) cracks armor.

hints.q: The rover cannot climb a ledge.
hints.a: Find the Spring Shocks on Redrock in Emberreach. Then Up makes the rover jump.

hints.q: A wall of rock blocks the way to a vault.
hints.a: Walk into it. Some rock is not rock at all, and crystal walls shatter at a touch.

hints.q: How do I reach the Maelstrom?
hints.a: Open the crystal gates in The Deep Black with the Sapphire and Amethyst shards; its jump ring leads to the Maelstrom.

hints.q: Something in the Maelstrom cannot be hurt.
hints.a: The Phantom, magma and tumbling asteroids cannot be hurt at all. Keep moving.

hints.q: The Guardian's seal won't open.
hints.a: Only the Core's own light opens it. Crack the Heart Eye three times: a plasma bolt or a shield orb does it cleanly, and ramming it works but hurts. Each time it reels away, then comes back faster. The third time its light flies to you, and the seal opens at a touch.

hints.q: Some say the felt-maker left something behind...
hints.a: Fly to where the galaxy chart's four corners meet. The chart wraps around, so all four corners are one place, as far from the Core as space goes.

hints.q: I'm there. It's just a knot of asteroids.
hints.a: Rock is not always rock. Try the knot's south face. And keep a module slot free: if you're full, drop one with O first.

hints.q: Plot me a course.
hints.a: Fly to the corner of the galaxy chart and come at the knot from below. The two rocks in the middle of its south face are only a picture: fly straight up through them. Inside, press G to pick up the felt egg, then touch the beacon.

items.title: Courier license
items.name: MAX
items.back: This courier carries the light of the galaxy. Every station, port and outpost shall grant safe docking and a hot meal. Couriers deliver.

items.title: Dispatch orders
items.letterhead: MAXIMA STATION · OFFICE OF THE STATION MASTER
items.body:
Max,

You have heard the news by now: the Core has cracked and the warp lanes are failing. Every courier on the ring has been grounded except you, because you are the only one who has flown all five sectors and come back with the cargo intact.

Your orders are simple and impossible. Find the ten star-shards. Carry them through the crystal gates, sector by sector. Fly the Maelstrom. Bring them home to the Heart.

The pod is fueled. The trading posts will take your credits. Hail anyone you meet; most of them will be glad to see a courier.

Couriers deliver. Deliver this one.

items.title: The Galactic Courier
items.headline: THE CORE GOES DARK
items.deck: Warp lanes failing sector by sector; ten star-shards scattered across the Hundred Worlds

photo.caption: Verdance, where the sky went dark first.

columns:
MAXIMA STATION - The Maximus Core, the forge-star that has lit the galaxy for ten thousand years, cracked at 0400 station time. Its light, held in ten star-shards, was flung across the Hundred Worlds.

Within the hour the lanes to Emberreach went quiet. By nightfall The Shallows had stopped answering.

"We have never lost a lane before," said a dock chief at the station, who asked not to be named. "Now we are losing them one after another."

The Courier Corps has grounded all but one pilot. Station sources confirm the courier known as Max has been given the job of bringing the shards home.

Traders at Waystation Ceres report pirate skiffs moving into the empty lanes. Couriers are advised to fly armed.

Crystal gates have reportedly sealed every sector beyond The Cradle. Scholars believe each gate answers only to its own pair of shards.
briefs: GLOOP SEASON EARLY
Verdance farmers report hopping slimes in record numbers. Harmless alone; never alone.
LIGHTHOUSE STILL TURNS
The old station in The Shallows keeps its light burning, though nobody has heard from its crew.
TRADING POSTS OPEN
Extra lives 100 credits, repairs 20, med kits 50. One of each per visit.

news.head: Maximus: 100 scenes, and not one more
news.html: Maximus: The Hundred Worlds is out. The Maximus Core has gone dark, and Max, a courier at Maxima Station, must carry ten star-shards home across 88 worlds by pod, on foot, by rover and in a diving bell. Game-Maker holds up to 231 scenes; we stopped at 100: a galaxy chart, five sector charts, 88 worlds, the Maelstrom, the Citadel and the Heart, plus a title, a training deck and an ending. Every limit we found is in LIMITS.TXT on the disk.

news.head: Courier’s corner
news.html: Registered couriers: your fold-out galaxy chart, the sector map of all 88 worlds and the hint book are in this box. Fold the chart along the creases and keep it by the keyboard.

news.head: Since last issue: GLITCH is gone
news.html: Virus Blaster pilots have been posting high scores on the BBS since July. Your favorite boss is the Feedback Howler; your least favorite is the Head Crash and its rings of platter shards. And the question everybody asks: can the BLASTER stop? No. The data stream never stops flowing. Pull Down to brake.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: A clown on the line
news.html: While we were building the hails in Maximus, a friend of the office asked to be in one. So on Boxcar Flats you'll meet Doc Leo, PhD (Comedic Science), a hobo clown with a rubber chicken on a leash. Doc Leo is a proud member of the Clown Club, twists balloon animals for the kids at every parade, and parks a little red electric car out front. He says he'll be in more games. We believe him.

news.head: In the workshop: Teddy gets a game
news.html: Remember Teddy, the SysOp's corgi? He's getting his own game, and it starts on the Fourth of July. Sandcastle Knight puts him in a tin helmet with a red plume as the knight of the backyard sandbox, with four castles to win back. Who knocked them down? Somebody with a lot of zoomies. You'll meet her next issue.

news.head: Letters: "Only in an emergency"
news.html:
"I told my mom I was shrinking down into the family 486 to fight a virus. She said to be home for dinner." - A pilot, by modem

The Scoop replies: Good advice. VACCINE.EXE is only for emergencies, and so is skipping dinner.

16.long: With the Dash Boots, dash left. With the Hydro Jets, burst left in the diving bell.

18.long: With the Dash Boots, dash right. With the Hydro Jets, burst right in the diving bell.

19.long: Use the Med Kit to mend hit points.

33.long: Fire the Hover Pack to rise while you hold the key.

34.long: Pick up what you are standing on.

44.long: Fire the Plasma Lance. It kills armor.

45.long: Fire the Nova Core: an eight-way burst.

57.long: Fire your blaster the way you last moved.

72.long: Fly up in the pod; on foot, fire your jets (tap again in the air to climb higher).

80.long: Fly down in the pod; on foot, curl into a ball.

1.long: Fire your blaster the way you last moved.

2.long: Pick up what you are standing on, or fire the Plasma Lance once you have it.

counters.20: Ruby shard

title: Meet the Monsters
author: Claude
blurb: Two short levels about monsters. One walks a path back and forth, one hurts a little when touched, and a mint green one pops when you land on it. Signs in the levels say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and change a monster.

box.back: A small explorer in a red beanie has two short levels to cross. A purple gumdrop waddles back and forth, a snail creeps along, and a mint green one is waiting to be dropped on. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and change a monster.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
Monsters walk a path, hurt a little, or pop
Made to be copied and taken apart

57.long: Jump. Steer with Left and Right while you are in the air.

counters.20: Keys: not used here, but a copy can add them.

title: Slide and Drift
author: Claude
blurb: Two short levels about momentum. Every step Yana takes adds to their speed instead of moving them, so they get faster while a key is held and glides on after they let go. A wall stops them at once. In the second level, a hop made at speed carries across gaps a standing hop cannot. Nothing here hurts. Signs explain each idea, and every level has a page on how it is made.

box.back: A small explorer in a pink beanie has two levels to cross, and every step adds to their speed. Hold a key and they get faster, let go and they glide on, press the other way and they slow. In the second level a run-up carries a hop across wide gaps. Signs say what each level shows, and the manual says how each is made.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
Momentum is one setting on a sequence in the character file
Made to be copied and taken apart

57.long: Hop. A hop made at speed, with Right still held, carries a long way.

72.long: Move up. Nothing here to climb.

75.long: Add to Kit's speed to the left. Hold it to go faster; let go to glide on.

77.long: Add to Kit's speed to the right. Hold it to go faster; let go to glide on.

80.long: Move down. Nothing here to climb.

counters.20: Keys: not used here, but a copy can add them.

title: The Mountain Moved Next Door
author: Claude
blurb: The day after Thanksgiving, Old Mossback, the mountain outside town, is sitting in the empty lot next door wearing half the street's garden gates, and the county survey crew comes at sunrise. Tess runs the trail crew. She has one day to find out why it came: put the gates back, climb its back, follow its footprints through the park and the library, cross a stream whose stones keep a schedule, gather the mist a nervous little cloud has dripped across a meadow, and outwit a squirrel who turns signposts. Then climb the old lookout at the last of the light, ride the wind over the ridge and the chimney smoke over the roofs, and light the tunnel. By night she walks a very embarrassed mountain home: clearing its way through the sleeping town, riding its waves across the ford and up the hill by moonlight. A story to play and to watch, here for a few days only.

title: Mustard Seed Hustle
author: The Bard of Bizarre
blurb: You are a mustard seed, the smallest thing in all the land, with the greatest feet. Hop out of your mound, lace up and hustle across the garden, push roots deep down in the dust for water, move a mountain with tiny faith and grow all the way up to the palm of God's hand. Shareware from The Sofa BBS, based on the song by The Bard of Bizarre, one of his gospel oddities (lyrics shaped by ChatGPT from Lewis Moten's prompt; music made with Riffusion, now Google Flow Music; animated cover made with Producer.ai, Riffusion's later name).
notice:
MUSTARD SEED HUSTLE
    Version 1.4 - September 1994
    by The Bard of Bizarre

"Oh, it's the mustard seed
 hustle, movin' slow but sure,
 Faith in the smallest things,
 that's the only cure!"

You are a mustard seed: the
smallest thing in all the land,

of your mound and across the

title: The Noodle Observatory
author: Claude
blurb: Monkey Day. A tin monkey rolls a lens into the kitchen telescope, a giant pasta ring rolls up the wall, and Nell finds a second moon in her window. She has already written to the paper; the letter runs Friday. Now she needs evidence: telescope parts from cupboards that tip, a ride up the pantry in the ring, lenses carried over gaps, nine shutters in the loft, a colander loose on the roof, and supper set where the view is best. Then the moon turns out to have a windowsill, the ring leaves with the tablecloth, and the night is only half over: snowy yards, a bakery with nobody home, a logbook by a round window, and the real moon, late as usual. A kitchen-sky mystery for about an hour, here for three days only.

pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
QUEST FOR THE ROUND TUIT

A Realm of Procrastia Adventure

In the Kingdom of Procrastia, everything gets done. Eventually. The castle in Laterburg has been waiting forty years for its roof. The bridge at Eventually Falls was started in the reign of King Dillydally VI. The Royal Library's overdue notices are themselves overdue.

What keeps the realm turning at all is the Royal Round Tuit: an old oak disc ringed in brass, kept on the Tuit Table in the Garden Court. Whenever a King of Procrastia gets a round tuit, he gets around to it. That's the law.

Then Lord Deadline, who hates a thing put off more than anything in the world, stole the Round Tuit, broke it in three and hid the pieces: one under the Snooze Barrows, one in the Soggy Vaults, one in the Putoff Mines. Without it, nobody in Procrastia gets around to anything. Least of all stopping him.

Nobody, that is, except Pip, the stable hand of Nowish, who does things the very day he's asked. His grandmother is very proud. And a little worried.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TUIT and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster plays the music and the digitized sound effects; without one, the PC speaker does its best.

Pick Play from the menu. Leave the menu alone and the game plays itself for a while: a good way to see how fighting works. Read Storyline tells the tale so far; Read Instructions is a short version of this manual.

Your satchel

There's nothing on the screen but Procrastia. Press F2 to open your satchel: it shows your gold, your hit points, your lives and what you carry. Save your game with F5 and load it with F6. Procrastia is bigger than it looks.

Hit points and lives

You start with 100 hit points, three lives and a single tonic. Foes bite; tonics, hearts, inn beds and the occasional pot put you right. Lose all your hit points and you start the place you're in over (with your gold and everything you've found still yours); lose all your lives and Lord Deadline wins. For now.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Controls

↑ ↓ ← →
or W A S D		Walk. Walk into people to talk to them, into counters to buy, into gates to open them.
SpaceSwing your sword the way you last walked. To face a boss (you can't walk into one), tap the arrow toward it, then swing. Once you own a steel sword, Space swings steel.
ZToot the Kazoo of Haste (once Doc Leo has taught you): a note flies straight ahead and beats nearly anything.
TDrink a tonic: 40 hit points.
EnterPick up what you're standing on. Hardly anything in Procrastia can be picked up. Hardly.
F1Help
F2Your satchel: gold, hit points, lives, what you carry
F3 / F4Music / sound effects on and off
F5 / F6Save / load
EscQuit to the menu

Driving THE CHEZ

On the Dawdle Flats the arrows drive (briskly) and Space squeezes the horn: its ah-OOO-gah flies ahead like a kazoo note and clears crabs off the causeway. Your hit points are the carriage's charge. Charging posts top it up.

pages.head: Townsfolk and Shops
pages.html:
Townsfolk and Shops

To talk to someone, walk into them. They'll have their say and you'll be standing just where you were. Talk to everyone: Procrastians know a great deal and get around to telling you most of it.

Shopping

Market stalls sell from their counters. Walk into a counter once to pay, and again to take what you bought. If you can't afford it, the counter won't budge.

Shops only keep a few of anything in stock. Leave town and come back; they'll have restocked. Eventually.

pages.head: The Kingdom
pages.html:
The Kingdom of Procrastia

Two lands across the Dawdle Flats, forty leagues of tidal mud nobody has ever finished walking.

Dallydale (the west)

  • Nowish: Pip's village. Population: some.
  • Laterburg: the capital. The Garden Court (roof pending), the market, the Procrastinating Pony, the Royal Library, the royal kennel.
  • Someday Harbor: on the west coast. The lighthouse, the long pier, the fishing pier, and Professor Fiddlesticks' garage.
  • The Whistling Woods, east of the River Dither, and Lake Later.

Far Putoff (the east)

  • Eventually Falls: a river town under a waterfall. Hattie's General Store, Doc Leo's tent, Foreman Duff.
  • Mount Putoff and its mines.
  • The Gloomwood, and in it Deadline Keep, where every clock has stopped at a minute to midnight.

pages.head: Old Procrastian
pages.html:
Old Procrastian

The old Procrastians carved their advice into floors, doors and anything else that would hold still, in runes nobody has read for four hundred years. Nobody got around to it.

The Royal Code Wheel reads them. Every carving begins with its key, set in brass: a letter, then a rune. Turn the small disc until the key's rune sits against the key's letter on the big disc. Now each rune of the carving sits against the letter it stands for. A blank stone is a gap between words.

Step on a carving's brass key to kneel and read it close up. Then take your time: the runes aren't going anywhere. They never have.

The miners' marks

The miners of Mount Putoff used the wheel's three windows. Set a key and the windows show three marks, 1, 2 and 3 from left to right. Miners hung their doors with marks, too. They meant to tell you why.

pages.head: Foes
pages.html:
Foes

Foes come at you when you're near. A bite hurts you, but it hurts them too. Two blows finish most of them; they leave a gem behind (5 gold, or a ruby worth 20). Some things in Procrastia leave hearts.

FoeWhereNotes
ProcrastislimeEverywhereWill attack you later. Later is usually now.
Snooze BatThe hills, the Barrows, the MinesQuick. One blow.
Barrow GhostThe Snooze BarrowsDrifts through rock. Wait for it to come out.
Tide CrabThe Vaults, the FlatsSideways, always. On the Flats some patrol the causeway, back and forth on a beat.
Bog EelThe Vaults' poolsLeaps from pool to pool.
Rust GolemThe Putoff MinesThree blows.
Gloom Goblin, Clockwork TickDeadline Keep (goblins also on the road south of Eventually Falls)The Keep's staff. Underpaid. On time.

Bosses

Each piece of the Tuit is guarded by someone two blocks tall who would rather be asleep: Sir Snoozalot, the Barrow King; the Kraken of Kinda-Later; Tick-Tock the Unpunctual; and Lord Deadline himself. Your wooden sword won't scratch the last three: buy steel. Bosses sit in the way. Swing until they aren't.

Lord Deadline

His clockwork armor is only the first half of the fight. Break it and Lord Deadline steps out on foot, sword up. He backs off a few paces, then charges straight at you, twice, before he backs away to think about it. Every moment he touches you costs hit points. Face the way he's coming and swing as he arrives, then step aside. Six good blows and he's done. The foes grow fiercer the deeper you go, so rest at an inn before the Keep.

pages.head: Hints
pages.html:
Hints from the Royal Library

  • Gates open for the right thing in your satchel: the Royal Writ (the Barrows), the foghorn (the fog bank on Someday Harbor's long pier), a lamp (the Mines), something with lightning in it (THE CHEZ's garage) and all three pieces (the Keep). Walk into them.
  • The King hands out writs to anyone who asks. Have two.
  • The Tuit Table in the Garden Court lights a pedestal for each piece you carry. A good way to check.
  • On the Dawdle Flats, the two low bridges flood with the tide. The tide pole beside each one counts it down: the water climbs the marks, the flag goes red, then the bridge is under. Wait for it to go out.
  • The rivers can't be swum. Look for bridges.
  • Shops restock whenever you come back to town.
  • Save before every boss.
  • Doc Leo's kazoo note beats nearly anything, but each toot costs a reed.
  • Runes in the floor? Step on the brass key in front of them to read them close up, and set the Royal Code Wheel by it.
  • Waterfalls are mostly water.

Stuck? The Royal Hint Book answers everything, under a sheet of red film. Free with registration.

pages.head: Credits
pages.html:
Credits

Design, pixels, maps, music, sound and words: Claude, at Sandbox Software. Every block, monster, song and scene is a real Game-Maker 3.0 file, built in code.

The shores, rivers and roads of Procrastia are autotiles: each block is chosen by which of its four corners lie in water, road, wood or rock, and each was painted in full color with antialiased edges, foam, wet sand and shadows, then dithered into the scene's 256-color palette.

Starring

  • Doc Leo, hobo clown, PhD (Comedic Science), as himself
  • Sir Reginald Cluckington III, a rubber chicken
  • Teddy, a corgi who knows his left from his right
  • Gwinn
  • THE CHEZ, a 1976½ CitiCar (charge port: rear passenger side)

For Lewis "Lewie" Moten III, who always gets around to it.

Made with GAME-MAKER by Recreational Software Designs.

pages.head: Registering
pages.html:
How to Register

Quest for the Round Tuit is shareware. Copy it for your friends, upload it to your favorite BBS, put it on a shareware disk: just keep all the files together and unchanged.

If you enjoy it, register for $15. You'll get:

  • the Cloth Map of Procrastia, printed on genuine imitation cloth,
  • the Royal Hint Book, with a sheet of red film to read the answers through,
  • the Royal Code Wheel, two discs of stout card and a brass fastener, for reading Old Procrastian,
  • the satisfaction of having got around to it.

Send a check or money order to:

Sandbox Software
P.O. Box 000
Pittsburgh, PA 15213

Please allow 4-6 weeks for delivery. Or, in Procrastia, 4-6 years.

news.head: Sandbox Software Gets Around to an RPG
news.html: Fans have asked for a role-playing game since our first disk. We said we'd get around to it. Quest for the Round Tuit is that. Four towns, four dungeons, two dozen people to talk to, and coastlines that curve - in Game-Maker, which nobody told us couldn't be done until we'd done it.

news.head: A horseless carriage in Procrastia
news.html: Every kingdom needs a way to get around. Procrastia's is THE CHEZ, a horseless carriage from the far-off future of 1976 and a half, waiting in Professor Fiddlesticks' garage for something with lightning in it. Charge it and drive forty leagues of tidal mud across the Dawdle Flats; its ah-OOO-gah horn clears the crabs off the causeway. Its charge port is on the rear passenger side, as always.

news.head: Since last issue: The box art made the printer
news.html: Depth Perception's box art went to the printer on time, and you've been pulling focus ever since. The trick most of you learned the hard way: a soft, see-through block isn't there right now. The trick most of you learned on the BBS: not every mirror in the Hall of Mirrors is a wall. And yes, registered players, the cardboard glasses are in your box. No, you won't need them.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Royal hounds
news.html: Teddy and Gwinn have royal jobs this time: they're the King's two runaway hounds, and Kennelmaster Bess would like them home. Doc Leo plays himself, as usual, and his rubber chicken finally has a name of its own. Office news: Gwinn sat on command this month. Once. Nobody had a camera, but three of us saw it.

news.head: In the workshop: Where's Gwinn?
news.html: The morning after the Big Show, Gwinn's bed is empty. That's how our next game begins: Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure. Teddy has a new trick, and for the first time in a Sandbox game you'll play as somebody else, too. Somebody big, brown and still learning to sit.

news.head: Letters: "Why ray tracing?"
news.html:
"My dad says ray tracing is for serious computers. Why is it in a game?" - A reader, by modem

The Scoop replies: Because a chrome sphere on a checkerboard is the most beautiful thing a computer can draw. Tell your dad the office 486 agrees, eventually.

items.title: A Royal Decree
items.letterhead: BY ORDER OF HIS MAJESTY KING DILLYDALLY IX
items.to: To whomever gets around to reading this
items.body:
Be it known that the Royal Round Tuit has been stolen by one LORD DEADLINE, who was not invited.

Any subject who returns the three pieces of the Round Tuit to the Tuit Table shall receive Our gratitude, a feast, and a Royal Writ (they are free; have several).

We shall see to the matter personally as soon as We get a round tuit. Which is, you will appreciate, the difficulty.

items.title: The Royal Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Compiled by Ms. Pagely of the Royal Library, who would like her books back. Lay the red film over an answer to read it.

hints.q: Where do I go first?
hints.a: North up the road from Nowish to Laterburg. Walk into the King on his throne at the top of the Garden Court: he gives you the Royal Writ.

hints.q: How do I talk to people?
hints.a: Walk into them.

hints.q: How do I buy things?
hints.a: Walk into the counter once to pay and again to take it. No money, no sale.

hints.q: I'm out of gold.
hints.a: Foes drop gems: 5 gold each, 20 for a ruby. The dungeons have chests. The kennel and the library pay rewards.

hints.q: The door in the Snooze Barrows won't open.
hints.a: It's sealed in the King's name. Get the Royal Writ from King Dillydally first, then walk into the door.

hints.q: How do I reach the Soggy Vaults?
hints.a: Walk out along Someday Harbor's long pier to the fog bank. It only clears for the Harbor Master's foghorn, which is lying in the west room of the Snooze Barrows.

hints.q: My sword bounces off the Kraken.
hints.a: From the Vaults on, bosses are too tough for wood. Buy the steel sword from Brokk in Laterburg's market for 80 gold.

hints.q: How do I get across to Far Putoff?
hints.a: In THE CHEZ. The second piece of the Tuit is full of lightning: carry it to Professor Fiddlesticks' garage in Someday Harbor and walk into the garage door.

hints.q: The bridge on the Flats is under water!
hints.a: It's the tide. Wait a few seconds and it drains again. The striped tide pole beside the bridge tells you when: once its flag goes red, the water is on its way.

hints.q: The Putoff Mines' door won't let me in.
hints.a: It wants a lamp: 40 gold at Hattie's stall in Eventually Falls.

hints.q: Lord Deadline jumped out of his armor!
hints.a: That's his second act. He backs off, then charges straight at you. Face him and swing as he comes, then step aside. Six blows; he leaves a heart.

hints.q: Where is Deadline Keep's door?
hints.a: On the south side of the Keep. The road from Eventually Falls goes round the east side of the Gloomwood to it.

hints.q: The Keep's sockets won't open.
hints.a: Each one wants its piece of the Tuit. If one stays shut, you're missing that piece: the Tuit Table in the Garden Court lights a pedestal for each piece you carry.

hints.q: How do I use the Code Wheel?
hints.a: Every carving starts with a brass letter and a brass rune. Turn the small disc until that rune sits against that letter. Then read each rune of the carving off the big disc.

hints.q: What do the runes in the Snooze Barrows say?
hints.a: Set rune Yawn against P: FOGHORN WEST. The foghorn is in the west room.

hints.q: Which door in the Putoff Mines?
hints.a: The miners' plate says M and rune Putter. Set them, and the windows show bell, lamp, gem: the third door from the west.

hints.q: What do the runes in Deadline Keep say?
hints.a: Set rune Snooze against D: SWING AS HE COMES. It's about Lord Deadline on foot.

hints.q: I picked a cupboard.
hints.a: No harm done: you come out in the passage south of the stopes. Walk back up and try the door the wheel shows you.

hints.q: Where are the royal hounds?
hints.a: Teddy is in a clearing in the Whistling Woods: take the trail east off the north road. Gwinn is digging on the beach south of Someday Harbor. Walk into each, then walk into the kennel gate in the Garden Court.

hints.q: Where is the Tome of Tomorrow?
hints.a: In the Putoff Mines' old workings, west of the great gallery. Take it to the rope at the Royal Library's door.

hints.q: Where is Sir Reginald Cluckington III?
hints.a: In a glade in the Gloomwood, east of the road to Deadline Keep. Walk into him, then into the flap of Doc Leo's tent in Eventually Falls.

hints.q: What does the kazoo do?
hints.a: Press Z. A note flies straight ahead and beats nearly anything, bosses included. Lyra sells reeds in Someday Harbor: ten notes for ten gold.

hints.q: The hermit's garden? What hermit?
hints.a: Eventually Falls has a waterfall at the top of town. Its left side is only spray: walk straight up through it.

hints.q: The nest is empty.
hints.a: Watch it. Every twenty seconds or so something turns up in it for a moment. Stand on the nest and press ENTER while it's there.

hints.q: Just draw me a map.
hints.a: Up the main street to the foot of the falls, through the left edge of the falling water, and into the garden. The nest is right of the hermit; the stone beside it opens for whoever carries the egg.

items.title: The Royal Code Wheel
items.note: Turns Old Procrastian runes into plain letters
items.heading: The Royal Code Wheel of Procrastia · Old Procrastian into plain letters
howto: Every carving in Procrastia begins with its key, set in brass: a letter, then a rune.
Turn the small disc until the key's rune sits against the key's letter on the big disc.
Now read the carving: each rune sits against the letter it stands for. A blank stone is a gap between words.
The three windows show the miners' marks for that key. Marks on a door read left to right: window 1, then 2, then 3.

puzzles.ask: The Snooze Barrows: what do the runes in the floor by the way in say?
puzzles.answer: FOGHORN WEST. The Harbor Master's foghorn lies in the barrow's west room. Take it before you go.

puzzles.ask: The Putoff Mines: which of the four doors in the bulkhead is the true one?
puzzles.answer: The windows show bell, lamp, gem: the third door from the west. The other three are cupboards.

puzzles.ask: Deadline Keep: what do the runes in the Hall of Sockets say?
puzzles.answer: SWING AS HE COMES. When Lord Deadline charges at you on foot, face him and swing as he arrives.

author: The Bard of Bizarre

title: Ride Along
author: Claude
blurb: Three short levels about a ride that keeps moving by itself. On foot, a small explorer walks into a parked rocket. The next level names a different character file: the rocket rises on its own, even when no key is held, and the arrows only steer it past rocks and between stars. The last level does the same trick in a canoe on a river that flows up the screen. Signs in the levels say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and make your own.

box.back: A small explorer climbs into a rocket that rises all by itself. Steer between the rocks, catch the stars and dock at the top, then take a canoe down a river that flows the same way. Each ride is a character file of its own. Play it, then open the game in Game-Maker and build your own.

title: Veni, Vidi, Risi!
author: Veni, Vidi, Risi!
blurb: I came, I saw, I laughed. In Rome nobody laughs at Marcus Iocundus's comic songs in Latin, and then, at his banquet for the senators, his dog Rufus breaks wind under the table. The Senate's sentence: make Emperor Gravis laugh (he hasn't in forty years) or count the sand of the Circus Maximus. So Marcus lives his six songs: throw open the shutters at the banquet, win a battle by running away (cucurri-curri-currimus!), cross the rooftops of Rome touching titles as a tongue twister twists them, hunt mice for cheese as Felix, the bravest cat, gather golden scales for the singing goldfish of the baths, and tell jokes at the theater until the stone faces crack and Emperor Gravis himself laughs, between his herald's hushes of SILENTIUM! Shareware from The Sofa BBS, from six Latin songs by Veni, Vidi, Risi!, Lewis Moten's group (lyrics shaped with ChatGPT from Lewis's prompts; music and vocals made with Riffusion, now Google Flow Music; title and cover art drawn for the game by Claude Opus 5.5).

    I Came, I Saw, I Laughed
    Version 1.5 - December 1994
    by Veni, Vidi, Risi!

"Omnes spectant, nemo ridet."
 (Everyone watches.
  No one laughs.)

Marcus Iocundus writes comic
songs in Latin, and nobody in
Rome laughs. Then, at his
banquet for the senators, his
dog Rufus breaks wind under
the table. The Senate's
sentence: make Emperor Gravis
laugh (he hasn't in forty
years) or count the sand of
the Circus Maximus. So Marcus
lives all six of his songs:
the banquet, a battle won by
running away, the rooftops of
Rome and a tongue twister,
the kitchen as Felix, the
bravest cat, the baths where
a goldfish sings, and at last
the theater, where nobody
laughs. Yet.

STARTING THE GAME
  Type RISI and press Enter.
  VGA required. A Sound Blaster
  is recommended for the music
  (an opera, a march, a patter
  song, an aria) and the sung
  Latin.

title: Road Tiles
author: Claude
blurb: Three short levels about drawing roads out of blocks. Level 1 is straight pieces and round corners that curve the road into the grass. Level 2 is a road that bends up onto a diagonal and down onto another, made of a band block and the corner triangles beside it. Level 3 lays one road across grass, sand and water, with a crossroads, a T, a blend block where grass runs into sand and a bridge. Signs name each piece, and the pages say how many blocks a set needs and how to draw each once and flip or turn it. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and look at the blocks.

manual.title: Sandcastle Knight - Teddy's Guide to the Sandbox

pages.head: The Zoomies of 1994
pages.html:
Sandcastle Knight

Pittsburgh, the Fourth of July, 1994. Behind a brick house on a hill sits a wooden sandbox, and it has a knight: Teddy, a Pembroke Welsh Corgi in a tin helmet with a red plume. He is low to the ground, big in the ears, and very, very good. Teddy knows lots of tricks, he loves his toys, and everybody on the street loves him.

He also has a big sister. Gwinn is a chocolate-brown pit-lab mix with amber eyes and a pink collar, twice his size, and she ruins everything. Never on purpose! She just has a lot of zoomies.

This morning she came through the sandbox at full speed. Every castle fell flat. She stepped on the hose and it ran into the moat, tipped the kiddie pool into a lagoon, dug a hole under the whole sandbox for the beetles to move into, and scattered Teddy's toys from one end to the other. Then she flopped down on the patio for a nap, right on top of the Crown of the Sandbox.

Pick up your shovel, Teddy. Rebuild the towers, raise the gates, gather your toys, and get your crown back from under your snoring sister.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Installing

Copy every file on this disk into one directory on your hard disk, for example C:\SANDCAST, and type SANDCAST. You need a 286 or better with VGA graphics and 640K of memory. All sound comes from the PC speaker, so no sound card is needed.

The title screen

The game dials up THE -= S A N D B O X =- BBS on its own (don't worry, your phone bill is safe) and shows the logon screen. Press any key for the menu:

  • Play starts a new game in the sandbox.
  • Read Instructions and Read Storyline show messages from the BBS message base.
  • See Highest Scores lists the Good Dogs of the Sandbox.

Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Teddy will show you around by himself. Pick Read Storyline to watch Gwinn's zoomies for yourself.

Your goal

Win back four castles, one in each corner of the sandbox, then face Gwinn. Each castle you win sets you down in the next corner, so the sandbox itself shows how far you have come.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Keys

Arrows or W A S DWalk (the numeric keypad arrows work too)
GPick up the thing you are standing on
SpaceFling a clod of sand (needs the shovel)
BThrow a splash of water (needs the bucket, and water in it)
FToss a tennis ball (you need to have found one)
F1Help
F2Status: score, hit points, lives, inventory and your sand
F4Sound effects on/off
F5 / F6Save / load a game
EscQuit to the menu

Tricks

Teddy knows his tricks. Show them off any time with the number keys along the top of the keyboard:

2Sit (and offer a paw)
3Spin! Twice round, kicking up a whirl of sand that bowls over any ant or beetle that runs into it
4Play dead
5Roll over

A joystick works as well: button 1 flings sand, button 2 throws water.

Thrown sand, water and balls fly the way you last walked, so take a step toward whatever you're aiming at first.

Counting your sand

The status screen (F2) counts your sand. Every scoop of sand you carry counts as one.

pages.head: Sand, Towers and Water
pages.html:
Sand

Sand is everything in this game. Pick it up by walking over a pile of wet sand: no key needed (G is for tools like the shovel and the bucket). With the shovel, walk into a dune to dig it: two bites and it is gone, and you keep the sand.

Spend sand by walking into things:

  • Tower rings (a circle drawn in the sand, with a little flag stake): one sand builds the tower. Walk into it again to plant your flag.
  • Anthills: one sand plugs the hole for good.
  • Fords (water with wooden stakes): one sand fills a square of the moat.

Gates

A castle gate lifts when you have planted its flags: four at Anthill Keep, two at the Hosewater Moat. The gate of the lagoon wants three golden shells instead.

Water

Once you find the bucket, water balloons and Gwinn's water bowls fill it, three splashes at a time. Only water can flip a crab. And with the bucket in hand, walk into a dashed outline in the sand to pack a wall of wet sand right there. Crabs can't get past a wall.

pages.head: Things in the Sandbox
pages.html:
ItemWhat it does
Pile of wet sandOne sand
Tennis ballOne toss (F). Gwinn will move for it. So will a crab.
Squeaky boneOne of Teddy's toys: 100 points
Flying discTeddy's best toy: 500 points
Golden conchOpens the lagoon's sea gate (you need three)
Dog biscuit40 hit points back
Peanut butterAn extra life
Water balloonThree splashes for your bucket
AcornOpens one root door underground
Floppy disk300 points (shareware!)
ShovelPick it up with G. Teddy carries it in his teeth: fling sand, dig dunes.
BucketPick it up with G. Throw water, pack walls.

Things that move you

  • Hose currents carry you along. You can step out sideways, but nobody walks upstream.
  • Crumbly sand bridges fall into the water behind you. Keep walking!
  • Waves roll up the beach and push you back to shore.
  • The tidal flat floods every so often. Wait it out on a sandbar.

pages.head: Who's Who
pages.html:
CreatureNotes
AntsPour out of anthills and run at you. One bite each. A clod of sand stops them; a scoop of sand plugs the hill.
BeetlesPatrol in lines and squares. Armored, but a clod of sand flips them.
CrabsScuttle back and forth. Walk into one and it pinches hard, once, and tumbles out of the way on its back. Sand bounces off; water flips them without the pinch. Or wall them in.
Hose dropletsThe garden hose spits them across the sand. Time your crossing.
GwinnTeddy's big sister: a brown pit-lab mix, twice his size. She galumphs around the sandbox and naps in doorways, and when she's on the loose she galumphs right past you (it doesn't hurt). Asleep in a doorway, she won't budge. Sand and water don't bother her a bit. Toss her a tennis ball and she trots off happy to bury it.
Slobbery ballsRoll out of Gwinn's mouth while she snores. They roll after you. Yuck.
Rope toysFly out of Gwinn's toy box. Too tough for sand; one bonk, and it's gone.
Gwinn, nappingSix blocks of sleeping big sister on the patio. Her left paw guards the path up her side, and her right paw lies across the crown. Splash a paw twice and she tucks it in; after the first splash, the right one starts swiping. When she snores, a gust blows down the path beside her and pushes you back (it doesn't hurt). The dust stirs and a Z drifts up just before.

Remember: Gwinn is not a bad dog. She is a good girl who knocks things over. Everybody loves her too.

pages.head: Tips: The First Castles
pages.html:
The Sandbox

Grab the shovel by the toy chest first. Anthill Keep is inside the ring of dunes: dig in. Grab the tennis ball next to the shovel, too.

1. Anthill Keep

There is more sand than you need. Plug the anthills near the towers before you build, and the ants will leave you alone. Gwinn is asleep across the doorway inside: walk up toward her and press F. Out of balls? Walk into the can of tennis balls beside her; it never runs out (there is one by her nap in the lagoon, too).

2. Hosewater Moat

The hose has cut the island in two, and each half has one tower ring. Two scoops of sand fill the south ford (the west bridge is free, but it only works once). Build the south tower, then ride the east current off the island. Round on the north bank, a current runs down across the moat to the north half. Build its tower, and the channel down the west side carries you back to the gate.

pages.head: Tips: Deeper In
pages.html:
3. Low Tide Lagoon

Pick up the bucket and a tennis ball near the start; Gwinn is napping in the only gap in the toy barrier. In the crab gullies, pack a wall on one side of the crossing while the crab is away. Cross the surf between waves, and grab the golden shells on the sandbars while the tide is out. The flat darkens and foams just before it floods. If it does, stand on a sandbar and wait.

4. Beetle Burrows

Three root doors and just enough acorns, plus one hidden behind a crack. Bring sand down with you for the ford over the underground stream.

5. Gwinn's Nap

Fill up at a bowl (they never run dry), take a step toward her left paw, and throw twice. Wait at the foot of the path while a snore blows past, then walk up. In the nook, splash the right paw again before its swipe reaches you, or step back down the path.

pages.head: Secrets
pages.html:
We won't tell you everything, but:

  • Not every little hole in the sandbox was dug by an ant. One of them dials a phone number.
  • Something in the courtyard of Anthill Keep leads very deep down, and back up again.
  • Cracked walls in the burrows are worth walking into.
  • Ride the hose's lazy loop in the southeast corner. Round and round.

THE -= S A N D B O X =- BBS was a real bulletin board in Pittsburgh, PA. This game is for everyone who ever logged on. Check the file area while you're there: the SysOp just uploaded a GIF of himself and his corgi.

items.title: Sandcastle Knight Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Find your question, then lay the red film over the answer. Good dogs only read one answer at a time.

hints.q: Where is the shovel?
hints.a: Right beside Teddy's toy chest in the southwest corner, where you start. Press G to pick it up.

hints.q: How do I get into Anthill Keep?
hints.a: Dig through the ring of dunes with the shovel. Two bites and a dune is gone, and you keep the sand.

hints.q: What is the tennis ball for?
hints.a: Gwinn moves for it. Walk toward her and press F, and she trots off happy to bury it.

hints.q: The gate of Anthill Keep won't open.
hints.a: Build all four towers (one sand each), then walk into each tower again to plant its flag. Four flags lift the gate.

hints.q: The ants keep biting me.
hints.a: Walk into each anthill with sand in your can: one scoop plugs it for good.

hints.q: How do I cross the Hosewater Moat?
hints.a: Two scoops of sand fill the south ford (the west bridge is free but crumbles after one crossing). Build the south tower, ride the east current out, then the north bank's current in to the north tower. The west channel carries you back to the gate.

hints.q: Sand bounces off the crabs.
hints.a: Water flips a crab without a pinch (walking into one pinches, once). Or, with the bucket, walk into a dashed outline to pack a wall the crab can't pass.

hints.q: The lagoon gate won't open.
hints.a: It wants three golden shells. They are out on the sandbars: grab them while the tide is out.

hints.q: There aren't enough acorns in the Burrows.
hints.a: One more acorn is hidden behind a cracked wall. Walk into the cracks.

hints.q: How do I get the crown back?
hints.a: Fill your bucket at a water bowl, take a step toward her left paw, and splash it twice. Walk up the path between snores, then splash the right paw twice before its swipe reaches you.

hints.q: The slobbery tennis balls keep rolling at me.
hints.a: Keep moving and fling sand at them; save your water for her paws.

hints.q: Some say the felt-maker left something behind in the sandbox.
hints.a: Gwinn was digging somewhere she shouldn't. Follow the paw prints.

hints.q: Where do the paw prints go?
hints.a: Way up in the northeast corner, above the way to Low Tide Lagoon, to one lone dune. Bring your shovel.

hints.q: Just show me where to dig.
hints.a: Pick up the shovel (G) by the toy chest. Go to the top right corner of the sandbox and follow the paw prints to the lone dune. Walk into it twice to dig it out, then step into the hole. In Gwinn's Dig, press G to pick up the felt egg. The little sandcastle by the ladder only lets you by once you carry it. Climb the ladder out.

items.title: A note from Gwinn
items.body:
i am sorry about the castles. And the hose. And the kiddie pool. And the hole. The beetles were already there i think.

i did not mean to sit on your crown. it was warm and the patio was sunny and i was so tired from the zoomies.

You can have the tennis ball back. It is under the tomato plants. It is a little wet.

You are the best brother and the best knight.

items.title: The Backyard Bugle
items.headline: ZOOMIES FLATTEN SANDBOX
items.deck: Four castles down, hose in the moat, crown missing; local corgi vows to rebuild

photo.caption: The scene this morning: the toy chest, a shovel and not one castle standing.

columns:
THE SANDBOX - Residents woke this morning to find every sandcastle in the backyard sandbox flattened. Witnesses describe a brown blur moving "very, very fast" shortly after breakfast.

The hose was left running into the moat. The kiddie pool is now a lagoon.

The suspect, Gwinn, a brown pit-lab mix, was later found asleep on the patio. She is believed to be lying on the Crown of the Sandbox.

"She's not a bad dog," said one neighbor. "She's a good girl who knocks things over."

Teddy, a Pembroke Welsh Corgi and the sandbox's only knight, has picked up his shovel. Asked about his plans, he sat, offered a paw, and rolled over.

Ants, beetles and crabs are said to be moving into the ruins.
briefs: TENNIS BALL MISSING
Last seen near the tomato plants. Reward: one belly rub.
MODEM HEARD AT NIGHT
Neighbors report squealing from the upstairs window. Probably the BBS.
WEATHER
Sunny. Low tide in the lagoon by noon.
