news.head: A corgi in a tin helmet
news.html: Teddy the Pembroke Welsh Corgi is the knight of the backyard sandbox, and in Sandcastle Knight he wins back four castles, his toys and the Crown of the Sandbox from under his snoring big sister. Dig dunes, plug anthills, build towers of sand and show off his tricks: sit, spin, play dead and roll over. It's the Fourth of July, so every knight who wins back the crown gets fireworks. No sound card needed: Teddy beeps along on the PC speaker.

news.head: Dial the sandbox
news.html: Not every little hole in the sandbox was dug by an ant. One of them dials our BBS, right inside the game, and your phone bill is safe. Have a look in the file area while you're logged on.

news.head: Since last issue: Couriers report in
news.html: Maximus couriers have been busy. The most-hailed world is Boxcar Flats (hi, Doc Leo). The most-asked question is about the star whales: every whale in a pod swims the same loop at the same moment, so a pod keeps its shape. Several of you have noticed that a pod in The Cradle spells a name. We aren't saying whose.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Meet Gwinn
news.html: Teddy has a big sister. Gwinn is a chocolate-brown pit-lab mix with amber eyes and a pink collar, younger than Teddy and twice his size, and she knows exactly one trick: zoomies. In her first week at the office she knocked over a coffee can of pencils, unplugged the modem and lay down on the SysOp's keyboard. She has never once sat when asked. Everybody loves her anyway.

news.head: In the workshop: Teddy's next adventure
news.html: Registered Sandcastle Knight players were promised the next Teddy adventure on disk, and it's on our workbench now: Teddy's Little Big Adventure. This time Teddy leaves the sandbox for the big town, with more tricks than ever and a friend of ours in a felt fedora. Your copy is on the house; watch the BBS for it.

news.head: Letters: "A galaxy on my monitor"
news.html:
"My Maximus galaxy chart is taped to the side of my monitor. Is that where it goes?" - A courier, by mail

pages.head: The Case
pages.html:
Final Curtain

An Inspector Ada Penn Mystery

Port Ellery, Saturday, October 31, 1936.

Opening night at the Paragon Theatre. The house is sold out for THE RAVEN'S BRIDE, a new melodrama written by, directed by and starring the Paragon's owner, Victor Crane.

In Act III, the bride Rowena (the lovely Lila Fontaine) stabs the wicked Count Corvin with a trick dagger, the kind whose blade slides into the handle. Victor Crane falls, as he has at every rehearsal. Six hundred people applaud.

He does not get up for his curtain call.

The dagger in his heart is real: an antique blade with a raven's head on the pommel. The audience has been sent home, the cast and crew are held in the green room, and the rain has not stopped. At half past ten a police car pulls up under the marquee, and Inspector Ada Penn of Homicide steps out.

She has until dawn.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type FINAL and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the digitized sounds; without one, the PC speaker does its best.

The Paragon appears in the rain. Press a key for the menu, then pick Play. Read Storyline shows the death scene again, and Read Instructions has the keys. Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Ada will show you around the box office and the wings herself.

Sergeant Dobbs meets you at the stage door and asks whose card the print on the trick dagger matches. The lab's fingerprint sheet in the box has the answer, if you look through the spyglass; step on a name to say. A wrong name costs nothing and neither does skipping it: walk to the door marked GO IN. The print only shows who held the prop, never who swapped it.

The case is told in five parts, and the card at the start of each one says which part you are in (PART 1 OF 5, and so on):

  • Act One, 10:30 PM. Search the empty theater with the house lights up.
  • The Green Room. Question the five suspects.
  • Act Two, 2:00 AM. Search again by the ghost light, with Mrs. Crane's keys.
  • The Green Room, 2 AM. Question them again and show them what you found.
  • Dawn. Name the killer on the stage.

F5 saves a case and F6 loads one. Save at the start of each part, and always before you accuse anyone!

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Controls

KeyWhat it does
Arrows or W A S DWalk
Q / EWalk up and to the left / up and to the right
Number pad 7 9 1 3Walk on the four diagonals
SpacePick up what you are standing on
ZLook through the lens (once you carry it)
F1Help
F2What you carry, your score, evidence and chances
F3 / F4Music / sound on and off
F5 / F6Save / load a case
EscGive up and go back to the menu

A joystick walks in all eight directions; its first button picks things up.

F2 is the status page: it counts your evidence and your chances.

pages.head: Searching the Paragon
pages.html:
Searching the Paragon

Evidence lies where it fell. Stand on it and press Space. Each piece rings a little chord and adds one to your evidence count.

Read the walls. Not everything can be carried. Notes pinned up and chalked on boards tell their own story: the bar's tab board, the box office count, the letter tucked in a dressing-room mirror, the playbill in Victor's office, the Historical Society's clippings in the lobby. Write down what they say.

Keys. Some doors are locked. A key goes on your ring when you walk over it, and is used up by the door it opens.

The green room door counts your evidence. Push it once and it takes your notes to look them over; push again and it gives them back and swings open. If you haven't found enough, it stays shut.

pages.head: Tools of the Trade
pages.html:
Tools of the Trade

The magnifying glass

The Paragon staged a Sherlock Holmes play two seasons ago, and the props room still has his glass. Carry it, and small things that nobody else would notice show up when you walk over them. Press Z to look through it.

It reads bad print, too. Push against a smudged word and the glass sets it right, one letter at a time.

The lantern

At 2 AM the power is off. Under the stage it is black as pitch: the floor and the walls only show where your lantern has been, one flagstone at a time. Listen for your footsteps, feel along the walls, and watch for red eyes.

Victor's safe

Three dials and a door. Push against a dial to turn it to the next symbol: a mask, a raven, a rose, a moon. Victor was a vain man who never wrote anything down that he could hang on a wall instead.

pages.head: Questioning
pages.html:
Questioning

In the green room, walk up to a suspect to sit down across the table from them. The floor holds question cards. Step on a card to ask that question; when they have answered, you are back in your chair to ask another. The EXIT card ends the talk.

The second time round, after Act Two, the cards carry the evidence you found: SHOW it to them and watch their faces.

The evidence board on the green room wall holds your notes on every piece you have found, and the coroner's report. Step up to a card to read it again.

People lie. Paper doesn't. When a witness and a piece of evidence disagree, believe the evidence.

pages.head: Who's Who
pages.html:
Who's Who

Name
Victor CraneOwner and star of the Paragon. Count Corvin. The victim.
Lila FontaineLeading lady: the Raven's Bride. She struck the blow.
Edgar BlissVictor's understudy. Played the Herald in Act I, then had the night off.
Agatha CraneVictor's wife, now his widow, and co-owner. Keeps the books.
Felix MorrowStage manager and prop master, thirty years at the Paragon.
Oliver PikeDrama critic of the Port Ellery Courier, in a complimentary seat.
Sgt. Walter DobbsYour sergeant. Holds doors. Makes coffee.
Commissioner HaleYour boss. Will not wait for a fourth guess.
MacbethThe theater cat. Not a suspect.

Things that go bump at 2 AM: the night watchman on his rounds (he won't let you past), the wisps from the ghost light (they cost you points), and the rats under the stage.

pages.head: Naming the Killer
pages.html:
Naming the Killer

At dawn the suspects stand in a row on the stage. Step into the spotlight in front of the one you accuse. If you are not ready, the BACK OFF card returns you to the green room.

Name the right one and they will ask you HOW it was done, and then WHY. Each is a choice of three cards. You need all three answers.

A wrong answer brings Commissioner Hale, who explains exactly why you are wrong, and gives you a strike. You have three chances: the third strike takes you off the case.

Scoring

  • Evidence: 100 points a piece; the hidden pieces are worth more
  • Opening the safe: 200
  • Reading the plaque in the lobby: 1,776
  • Solving the case: 5,000
  • A wrong answer: -500
  • Every scare costs a few points

items.title: The Port Ellery Courier
items.headline: STAR SLAIN ON STAGE
items.deck: Victor Crane falls in Act III of his own play; the dagger was real. Police hold cast at the Paragon.
columns:
PORT ELLERY, Oct. 31. - Six hundred playgoers at the Paragon Theatre tonight applauded what they believed was the finest death scene of the season, only to learn that Victor Crane, 52, the theater's owner and the star of its new melodrama, THE RAVEN'S BRIDE, was in fact dead.

Mr. Crane, as the villainous Count Corvin, was struck at 9:48 by the heroine Rowena, played by Miss Lila Fontaine, with what should have been a harmless stage dagger.

Police say the weapon was a genuine antique blade. Inspector Ada Penn of Homicide arrived shortly after ten and ordered the company held in the theater's green room.

Mrs. Agatha Crane, the widow and co-owner, declined to comment. The play's second performance has been canceled. Mr. Edgar Bliss, Mr. Crane's understudy, is expected to assume the role when the house reopens.

OUR CRITIC'S VIEW. The Courier's drama critic, Mr. Oliver Pike, was in attendance. His review, filed before the tragedy was known, will not be printed. Of the play itself Mr. Pike remarked only that it was "rather good. Surprisingly good, for Victor."

briefs: Rain to continue
The weather bureau promises rain through Tuesday.
Ghost light burns on
Theater custom keeps one bulb lit on an empty stage all night.

History in the lobby
The Historical Society's archives committee has hung its July 1776 plaque and old Courier clippings at the Paragon.
Correction
A 1931 item in these pages printed a new play's title as "Rayen Brine." The Courier regrets the error, five years late.
For sale
Remington Noiseless typewriter. Types without a sound, which some find unnerving. $75. Box 1936.

hints.q: Sergeant Dobbs asks whose card the dagger's print matches.
hints.a: Lila Fontaine's, the first name. The lab sheet's lifted print is her round whorl, turned and smudged. A wrong card costs nothing, and the GO IN door is open either way.

hints.q: Where do I start?
hints.a: The box office, off the west side of the lobby. There is a key on the floor and the seating chart on the desk.

hints.q: How do I get backstage from the house?
hints.a: Take the west aisle to the front, then go up through the pass door in the corner at stage left.

hints.q: Victor's office is locked.
hints.a: The key from the box office opens it. Walk into the door.

hints.q: I have three pieces of evidence and can't find a fourth.
hints.a: Get the magnifying glass from the props room shelves, then walk the floor in front of the prop table in the stage-right wing.

hints.q: The green room door won't open.
hints.a: It needs all four pieces of Act One evidence: the seating chart, the checklist, the ticket stub and the insurance policy. Push it, then push again.

hints.q: It's too dark under the stage.
hints.a: Get the night watchman's lantern from the WATCH room at the east end of the corridor. Everywhere you walk lights up.

hints.q: How do I get under the stage?
hints.a: Through the pit gate on the east side of the front rail, along the orchestra pit, and through the PIT door.

hints.q: What is the safe's combination?
hints.a: The playbill on the office wall: RAVEN, ROSE, MOON, left to right. Push each dial until it shows its symbol.

hints.q: Where is the fourth piece in Act Two?
hints.a: Beyond the trap room maze: a doorway in its far south-east corner, open only tonight, leads into the old prop vault. The rats are harmless, but they cost you points.

hints.q: The watchman keeps getting in my way.
hints.a: He only walks the south half of the corridor. Keep to the north side.

hints.q: Who has an alibi?
hints.a: Lila (Mrs. Hobbs), Edgar (the bar tab chalked at 9:05 and 9:15), Agatha (the box office count signed 9:10) and Felix (his crew). One suspect has nobody to vouch for him.

hints.q: Who lied?
hints.a: The critic. He says he never left seat F-9, but his stub was under the prop table and his umbrella left the cloakroom at 9:05.

hints.q: What does the clipping in the lobby say?
hints.a: It's a misprint. Carry the lens and push against each smudged word: PIKE'S PLAY: RAVEN BRIDE, back in 1931.

hints.q: Is the plaque worth reading?
hints.a: Exactly 1,776 points' worth. Push against its middle.

hints.q: Who did it?
hints.a: Oliver Pike, the critic.

hints.q: How?
hints.a: He swapped the trick dagger for a real one at the prop table during the interval. There was no poison, and the Act III blackout had been cut.

hints.q: Why?
hints.a: Victor Crane stole his play. Pike wrote THE RAVEN'S BRIDE in 1931; the manuscript was in Victor's safe.

hints.q: Some say the felt-maker left something behind in the theater.
hints.a: Somewhere comfy, and only after midnight. Bring your magnifying glass.

hints.q: Where, after midnight?
hints.a: The green room, at 2 AM. The sofa looks like any sofa, until you look closer.

hints.q: I give up. Spell it out.
hints.a: At 2 AM, carry the magnifying glass from the props room into the green room. Stand just left of the sofa in the bottom right corner and push right into it (it costs one lens charge). The egg shows between the cushions: push again to take it, then step into the empty seat.

Stuck in the dark under the stage? Can't crack Victor's safe?

The FINAL CURTAIN HINT BOOK answers every question you might have, from the box office to the curtain call, printed under red ink so you only read the answer you need. Comes with its own red decoder film, a floor plan of the Paragon and the full solution, sealed.

FREE with registration ($15), or $5 on its own. Fill in the order slip in the box.

items.title: A note found in the green room
items.body:
You will remember the play. You laughed at it in this very office five years ago. Tonight six hundred people will see it with your name on the program.

Enjoy your death scene.

news.head: Final Curtain: our first whodunit
news.html: Port Ellery, Halloween night, 1936. Six hundred people watched Victor Crane die in Act III of THE RAVEN'S BRIDE and thought it was acting. In Final Curtain you are Inspector Ada Penn of Homicide, and you have until dawn. Search the Paragon with the house lights up, then again by the ghost light; question five suspects, then show them what you found. Name the killer, how and why. Commissioner Hale gives you three chances.

news.head: Since last issue: The Big Show went on
news.html: Teddy's Little Big Adventure is the most-played game on our BBS this summer. Play dead is still the favorite trick (it's the only way past the Pie-O-Matic), and the most-asked question is how high a corgi can hop. Two blocks easily, three with good steering, four never. A wall that tall always has another way around.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Trick or treat
news.html: On Halloween night Doc Leo will be at the office door with balloon animals for the trick-or-treaters: dogs, swords and, by special request, one very long giraffe. Teddy is going as a knight again. Gwinn is going as Gwinn; she ate the other costume. THE CHEZ is going as a pumpkin, which, being tomato red, it already mostly is.

news.head: In the workshop: A library in a box
news.html: Remember the Dog House, the tiny red lending library on a post on Maple Street in Teddy's adventure? We looked inside. It's much bigger than the box. KEEP IT BRIEF! is about the night every word fell out of every book, and the tin night librarian who has to put them back, exactly one hundred words at a time.

news.head: Letters: "Is the Clown Club real?"
news.html:
"Teddy, Gwinn, Doc Leo, the Big Show... is the Clown Club real?" - A reader, age 9

The Scoop replies: Very real. Doc Leo marches in its parades, and the Clown Club puts on shows for kids all over town. In real life there are fewer custard pies.

title: Slow Computers
author: Claude
blurb: Three short levels about what made a game slow down on an old PC. Level 1 has a short pad and a long pad: a sound was read from the disk whole before the game went on, so a long one froze the game while it loaded, and the music kept its own time. Level 2 puts 36 friendly monsters on one screen, which a 286 could not keep up with. Level 3 moves the whole sky every tick. A player with a speed setting can run it like a 286, a 386 or a 486 and see the difference. Signs and pages give the numbers as estimates, and tips for keeping a game fast. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and change a sound or count the monsters.

box.back: A small explorer finds three short rooms that show what slowed a game down on a 1994 PC: a long sound that freezes the game while it loads, a crowd of monsters, and a sky that moves every tick. A player with a speed setting can run it like a 286, a 386 or a 486. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and change a sound.

Scream at the fog machines, tackle a papier-mache witch ("GET DOWN!") and say sorry, strategically reposition away from the guy in the werewolf mask through a wall of fake spiderwebs, buy the $12 souvenir sword, defend yourself from an 11-year-old in a cardboard knight costume, and bond with the emergency exit sign. Lily gets the Bravery Badge. pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
SNOWBOUND

The $89 Shovel

Fort Ashby, Mineral County, West Virginia. Friday, December 11, 1992.

The storm came in overnight and left a foot and a half of snow on the neighborhood. School is closed. The Mineral County Courier says the whole county is snowbound.

You have a shovel, a coffee can, and a plan. Over at LaVale Mall, in the window of Bits & Bytes Software, sits a pink box: GAME-MAKER, the kit that lets you design your own worlds, monsters and music without programming. It costs $89. In January it goes up to $129. Just down the hall is Bleeps, the arcade, where you spend every Saturday you can.

So this morning you hung out your sign at home, on the corner of Gale Street and Dunn Drive: Moten Snow-to-Software Operations, founder and operator. One dollar a scoop. Every driveway is a pixel of the game you are going to make.

Dig out your street, sled down Jamie Street, work Bowden Drive, and get to the mall before closing time. The box is yours.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type SNOWBND and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster plays the music and the digitized sound effects; without one, the PC speaker beeps along.

From the menu, pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute to watch a demonstration. Read Storyline shows the morning paper; Read Instructions is a short version of this manual.

The coffee can

There is no money counter on the screen - real shovelers don't have one either. Press F2 any time to tip out the coffee can and count it: the status screen shows your dollars, warmth and lives. You need $89 when you reach the register.

Warmth and lives

You start with 100 points of warmth and three lives. Plows, cars, carts, snowballs, a playful dog and the town bully all wear you down; hot cocoa warms you back up. If you get too cold you go home, warm up, and start that street over - with every dollar you've earned still in the can.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Controls

↑ ↓ ← →
or W S A D		Walk. Walk into deep snow to shovel it.
Q E
keypad 7 9 1 3		Walk diagonally: Q up-left, E up-right; the number pad corners go all four ways. Holding two arrows at once won't do it - use these.
SpaceThrow a snowball the way you last walked.
EnterPick up what lies at your feet.
F1Help
F2Count the coffee can (money, warmth, lives)
F3 / F4Music on/off, sound effects on/off
F5 / F6Save / load a game
EscQuit to the menu

On the sled

← → or A DLean and steer. The sled drifts - steering builds up sideways speed.
↑ or WDig in your heels to slow down (hold it and you'll creep back uphill).
↓ or SPush off - one shove each time you press it. Tap it to get going again after a crash.
Q EBrake and steer left or right at the same time.

A joystick works too: directions walk or steer, either button throws.

pages.head: Shoveling
pages.html:
Shoveling for Dollars

Plain yard snow is just snow. The big, puffy deep snow heaped on driveways and front walks is work - and work pays. Walk into a heap and you scoop it: $1 a scoop, and the pavement underneath is clear.

Don't forget the front walks

Every neighbor wants the front walk cleared too - to reach the car, fetch the paper off the door mat, and keep Grandma from slipping on the steps. That's more scoops - and more dollars - at every house.

Things worth picking up

  • Dollar bills - $1. They blow all over the Jamie Street hill and the frozen creek.
  • A tip envelope - $5, left on a porch by a happy customer.
  • Hot cocoa - warms you up by 35. Outside Bleeps it's root beer instead: the snack bar sells nothing else.
  • Plow banks - the dirty heaps the plows leave along the road. Scoop one to pack more snowballs.

Snow forts

Kids behind snow forts lob a snowball every few seconds. Walk right into a fort to knock it flat (100 points) and it stops throwing - then shovel the pile it leaves for $2.

pages.head: Hazards
pages.html:
Who's Out in the Snow

SnowplowsThe state crews never stop. A plow fills a whole lane; cross the road behind it, never in front.
CarsThe far lane of Bowden Drive is busy when everybody comes home from work.
SnowballsFrom the forts. They home in on you, but they're slower than you are and melt after a couple of seconds. Your own snowballs knock them out of the air.
BiscuitThe friendliest dog in Fort Ashby. When you get close he runs straight at you, knocks you flat, and bounds off happy.
Big PeteThe bully. He follows you around, gives you one good shove, and strolls off pleased with himself - then comes looking again a few seconds later. A snowball gets him first: he strolls off without the shove.
Fire hydrantsBuried up to the cap. You can't shovel through one - walk around.
Shopping cartsLoose in the mall lot, rolling wherever the wind takes them.
IceSlides you the way its arrows point. The creek along Bowden Drive runs east and will carry you along if you cross on the ice instead of the bridge.

pages.head: The Six Streets and the Mall
pages.html:
From Sunrise to Closing Time

1. Gale Street - 7:00 AM

Your own street, pink with morning. Home is at Gale Street and Dunn Drive - Dad already dug out ours. Three neighbors along Gale and two more up Leota Street need their driveways and front walks dug out - about $49 with the tip. You are subbing on the News-Tribune route this morning, too: grab the bundle by the porch at home and leave a paper on each customer's door mat for 250 points. One plow works Gale, Biscuit is loose in the park, and a practice fort waits behind the fence. When you're done, head east to Leon Drive.

2. Jamie Street - Noon

Leon Drive brings you to the top of Jamie Street, closed for sledding: the longest run in town. The hill bends to the right all the way down, past three stands of trees: snowy firs and red and blue gates at the top, white birches in the middle, and the lamps of lower Jamie Street at the bottom, where somebody has strung Christmas lights on the firs. Boards in the trees on both sides count down from 9 to 1 as you go. The snow is banked up along the edges and nudges you back toward the middle, and where the run squeezes between trees, ripples in the snow point the way round and carry you with them. Steer around the rocks and trees, slow down on the moguls, and grab the dollars blowing down the run. Kids on toboggans cut across without looking. Past the last board there is one more steep drop between the lit firs, and then the checkered finish, with the street lamps of Bowden Drive lit just below it, drops you at the corner of Jamie and Bowden.

3. Bowden Drive - 4:30 PM

A long row of houses, everybody home from work - and most of them got the shovel out themselves. Two north-side neighbors still want a clear path from the car to the door, and two more wait across the frozen creek, down the paths through the pines. Take the footbridge over (the ice carries you east), and watch for Big Pete, who hangs around it. Two plows and a car share the road. The sign at the east end points the way to LaVale.

4. LaVale Mall - 8:00 PM

Night, lamps, and a parking lot full of buried cars of every color, in three rows with a lamp island in the middle of each. Lost? A lit sign at the far right edge of the lot points back to the mall. Every twenty seconds or so a squall blows through and the lot fills back in - shovel it again and the money keeps coming. Meltwater has frozen along the back of the lot into an icy lane that slides you east toward the stores. You'll need the lot: the streets alone rarely add up to $89, so count on the lot for the last $15 or $20, with the plows on the fire lane, the carts loose and Big Pete about. Bleeps, the arcade, is near the middle of the mall: every push on its door costs $1 for a game, worth 100 points and a little warmth. Bits & Bytes is at the right end. The register only opens with $89 in your can. Out front, a History Fair table has a Liberty Bell - push it to ring it for 1776 points.

pages.head: Tips
pages.html:
Tips from the Founder

  • Shovel up a driveway, not across it: you clear one column per trip.
  • Check F2 before you leave a street. Whatever you're short, the LaVale Mall lot makes up - and every dollar from the streets is one less scoop in the dark.
  • Throw a snowball at a homing snowball - yours always wins.
  • The plow banks along every road are free ammunition. Keep your pockets full before you walk into the park.
  • On the sled, brake before the tree islands, not in them. If you stop dead, push off with ↓.
  • Jamie Street bends right. Lean right now and then to stay in the middle, and let the banked snow and the ripples carry you round the squeezes.
  • When the mall lot starts to dust over, get in the open: the heavier the squall, the more scoops within reach.
  • If you go home cold, the street starts over with fresh snow - and fresh money. Your coffee can stays full.
  • Bleeps is tempting. Play all you want - the lot keeps snowing - but count the can before you head for the register.

pages.head: Credits
pages.html:
Credits

Design, pixels, levels, music and sound: Claude

Every block, monster, character, song and sound effect in SNOWBOUND was built as a genuine Game-Maker 2.0 file: four levels, 135 background blocks, 30 monster pictures, 23 kinds of monster, two characters drawn in 20 poses, nine Sound Blaster songs, fourteen digitized sounds and an Autodesk Animator FLI intro.

Made with GAME-MAKER by Recreational Software Designs.

For the founder and operator of Moten Snow-to-Software Operations, Fort Ashby, winter of 1992, who shoveled his way to a copy of Game-Maker at LaVale Mall - one driveway, one pixel at a time. See you at Bleeps.

items.title: Jamie Street sled run poster
items.heading: JAMIE STREET SLED RUN
items.intro: Closed for sledding. Top to bottom in one go: the longest run in town.

panels.caption: The whole run as you ride it, top to bottom. Start at Leon Drive at the top of picture 1 and ride down; each picture carries on at the top of the next, where the numbered rings match. The street goes round the edges of the town map, so each lap is fresh hill: the firs, then the birches, then the lamps and lit firs, with the boards counting down 9 to 1 and the finish above Bowden Drive at the end of the last picture.

items.title: Snowbound Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: From the founder's own notebook. Lay the red film over an answer to read it.

hints.q: How do I know how much money I have?
hints.a: Press F2 to tip out the coffee can: the status screen shows your Money.

hints.q: I got to the register without $89.
hints.a: Go back out to the mall lot. A squall blows through every twenty seconds or so and buries it again: more scoops, more dollars. The streets alone rarely add up to $89.

hints.q: Where are the tips?
hints.a: A $5 envelope beside Mrs. Haines' porch on Gale Street.

hints.q: What are the door mats on Gale Street for?
hints.a: The morning paper. Grab the bundle by the porch at home, dig out each walk, and step on the mat: 250 points a paper.

hints.q: What is a snow fort worth?
hints.a: Walk into it to knock it flat for 100 points, then shovel the pile it leaves for $2.

hints.q: How do I leave Gale Street?
hints.a: Head east to Leon Drive at the end of the street; it leads north to the top of Jamie Street.

hints.q: I keep crashing on the sled.
hints.a: Brake with Up before the tree islands, not in them. If you stop dead, push off with Down. The run bends right, so lean right now and then to keep to the middle, and let the ripples in the snow carry you round the squeezes.

hints.q: How long is the Jamie Street sled run?
hints.a: Three stands of trees: firs, birches, then the lamps and lit firs of lower Jamie Street. The boards in the trees count down from 9 to 1. After the 1 comes a last steep drop between the lit firs, then the finish line above Bowden Drive.

hints.q: The creek ice carries me away.
hints.a: It runs east. Cross on the bridge instead of the ice.

hints.q: Big Pete won't stop shoving me.
hints.a: He shoves once, strolls off and comes back a few seconds later. A snowball sends him off before he can shove. Scoop a plow bank for more snowballs.

hints.q: What does the bell at the mall do?
hints.a: Push it. It rings for 1776 points, once, and swings the rest of the night.

hints.q: Homing snowballs keep hitting me.
hints.a: Throw one of your own at them: yours always wins.

hints.q: I'm freezing.
hints.a: Grab hot cocoa, or the root beer outside Bleeps (35 warmth each). If you go home cold, the street starts over with fresh snow, and your coffee can stays full.

hints.q: Some say the felt-maker left something behind...
hints.a: The snowman behind your house lost a mitten. Where a mitten drops, a trail starts.

hints.q: I found the mitten. Now what?
hints.a: The pine right behind it is only painted on. Walk straight through it and follow the trail into the woods. What you can't push, stoop for with Enter.

hints.q: Just draw me a map.
hints.a: In the park across Gale Street, find your snowman at the bottom of the park and the red mitten just below it. Walk down into the pines there: the trail runs down, right and down again to a hollow. Press Enter on the felt egg to pick it up, then push the frozen toboggan for a ride to Jamie Street.

items.title: The Mineral Courier
items.headline: AREA SNOWBOUND
items.deck: Foot and a half overnight in Mineral County; schools closed; plows out on every road

photo.caption: Gale Street at dawn: one driveway done, the rest waiting.

columns:
FORT ASHBY - A storm that came in overnight left a foot and a half of snow across Mineral County, closing schools and sending state plow crews out on every road before dawn.

Residents of Gale Street, Dunn Drive and Leota Street woke to find cars buried to the mirrors.

Neighbors want front walks cleared as well as driveways. "Grandma's coming at noon and my steps are a skating rink," one Leota Street resident said. "Somebody is going to make a fortune today."

Jamie Street is closed to traffic and open to sleds.

Over the line in LaVale, Maryland, stores plan to open on time. The Bleeps arcade promises the heat will be on.

A local software shop reports one copy of a popular game-making kit left in the window at $89. The price goes up in January.
briefs: SHOVELING FOR HIRE
A sign has gone up at Gale and Dunn: one dollar a scoop, founder and operator on duty.
HYDRANTS BURIED
The fire department asks residents to dig out hydrants near their homes.
FORECAST
Clearing by noon. Squalls near the mall after dark.

entries.html: Papers out (subbing on the route again). Sign is up. Coffee can is empty. Goal: $89 before the mall closes.
Gale Street done. Mrs. Haines tipped $5! Leota next.
Jamie Street is closed for sledding. Fastest way to Bowden. Lost my hat on the moguls.
Bowden Drive. Big Pete again. Snowball solved it.
LaVale lot keeps filling back in. Good. Count: almost there. DO NOT spend it all at Bleeps.

items.title: Business card
items.name: THE FOUNDER
items.back: Driveways, front walks, plow banks and fire hydrants. Every driveway is a pixel of the game I'm going to make.

items.title: Thank-you letter
items.body:
Thank you for registering SNOWBOUND. You helped a kid with a shovel buy a pink box, and that pink box made this game.

As promised, your printed map of Fort Ashby is in this box, along with the hint book and a few things from the founder's coffee can.

SNOWBOUND II: Spring Thaw is next: mud season, a lawn mower, and a used 486 at the flea market. Watch The Sandbox Scoop and the BBS for news.

We promise to keep making games.

news.head: Snowbound: how Sandbox Software began
news.html: Hello, and welcome to the very first Sandbox Scoop. Fort Ashby, West Virginia, Friday, December 11, 1992: a foot and a half of snow, no school, and a pink box in the window of Bits & Bytes Software at LaVale Mall: GAME-MAKER, $89 until January. Snowbound: The $89 Shovel is the true(ish) story of how this company was paid for, and our first game. Dig out the neighbors’ driveways at a dollar a scoop, deliver the papers, sled down Jamie Street and get to the register before closing time. Mind Biscuit. He is very friendly.

news.head: SNOWBOUND II: Spring Thaw
news.html: The snow is melting in Fort Ashby, and the founder has a new plan: mow lawns all through mud season. Registered SNOWBOUND players get it free when it’s done.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: A company started with a snow shovel
news.html: This company was paid for one driveway at a time. When the big storm closed school on December 11, the founder shoveled the neighborhood at a dollar a scoop until there was enough for a copy of GAME-MAKER. Christmas vacation did the rest. The office is a desk, the family 286 and a stack of graph paper. The shovel is in the corner, in case we ever need another program.

news.head: In the workshop: The future, as we see it
news.html: Everybody knows what the year 2000 will be like: flying cars, robots everywhere and dinner in a pill. Our next game goes there to find out. In In The Year 2000! a kid and his robot dog have until 3:00 to get a science report to the Fair. The robot dog is the problem.

news.head: Letters: The mailbag is empty
news.html: This is issue 1, so nobody has written to us yet. Be the first! Tell us how many dollars you scooped, which hill you sledded best, and whether Biscuit got you. The first letter we get goes right here.

pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
TEDDY'S LITTLE BIG ADVENTURE

A little dog. A big town. A ton of tricks.

Teddy is a Pembroke Welsh Corgi. He is short. He is fluffy. He has the most famous rump on the block, and he knows a ton of tricks.

His person is Doc Leo, a friendly hobo clown with a chewed-up felt fedora, wire glasses, a painted-on ash beard, a green tie and red sneakers. He walks a rubber chicken on a dog leash. Doc Leo is a proud member of the Clown Club: he twists balloon animals, does magic tricks - there is always a dove in that hat - and marches in every parade in town. Tonight is the Clown Club's Big Show. Guess who the star is.

Teddy also has a big sister. Gwinn is a chocolate-brown pit-lab mix, younger than Teddy but twice his size. She was adopted, and she is still learning: she has never once sat when asked. She knows one trick, and it is zoomies. This morning Doc Leo drove ahead to the Clown Club in his little red CitiCar and left his costume suitcase on the back step. Gwinn found it, ran off with it, and galloped all over town. The fedora, the green tie, the red sneakers, the rubber chicken and the red nose went flying, and his balloon dogs floated away.

No nose, no show! Doc Leo is already at the Clown Club. Only a little dog can save the Big Show.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TEDDY and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the digitized woofs, yips and honks; without one, the PC speaker beeps along gamely.

A cartoon plays first: watch Gwinn make off with the suitcase (pick Read Storyline to see it again). Press any key to get to the menu, then pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Teddy will show you around the backyard himself.

There are five stops on Teddy's adventure. Before each one, a card shows which stop it is (LEVEL 2 OF 5), where you are, which piece of Doc Leo's costume to look for, and which trick is new. At the end of every stop, Doc Leo's friend Pockets waits with the Clown Car. Bring him the costume piece and the door pops open: hop in and he drives you to the next stop.

Energy and naps

Teddy starts with 100 energy (the F2 screen calls it Hitpoints) and three naps (Lives). Pests and flying things wear him down; a bone gives 25 back, and Teddy's green wobble ball is worth a whole extra nap. When his energy runs out Teddy is tuckered out and naps; he wakes at the start of the stop he was on. When all the naps are used up, the game is over.

Press F5 to save your game and F6 to load it.

pages.head: Moving and Hopping
pages.html:
Moving and Hopping

Left Right
or A D		Walk. Teddy turns to face the way he is walking.
Up or WHop! Tap it for a little hop, hold it to hop higher. Let go of Up and Teddy goes back to walking, so to hop onto something, hold the arrow key toward it, press Up, and let go of Up when you are high enough.
Q EHop up and to the left (Q) or right (E) in one go. Holding Up and Right together won't do it - use Q and E, and hold them as long as you would hold Up.

How high can a corgi hop?

Two blocks easily. Three blocks if you hold Up the whole way and steer at just the right moment: Teddy scrambles up anything he can get his front paws over. Four blocks, never. Walls that tall need another way around, and there always is one.

Ledges

Awnings, branches, clotheslines, bridges and tightropes can be hopped up through from below and stood on from above.

Things that lift

Fountain jets, subway steam vents, trampolines and the Clown Club's stage lift push Teddy up into the air. Walk into one, ride it up, and steer off the top.

pages.head: Teddy's Tricks
pages.html:
Teddy's Tricks

Teddy knows a ton of tricks, and every one of them is good for something. The five he learns on the way are on the number keys along the top of the keyboard, in the order he learns them.

SpaceSpeak. WOOF! The bark rolls ahead the way Teddy faces (after a hop, it goes up). Squirrels, cats, pigeons and geese clear right out. Barking is the only thing a cat napping in a doorway respects.
DownDig. Digs up the block under Teddy's feet: bones sticking out of the lawn pop right out, and soft dirt or sawdust (look for paw prints) gives way to a tunnel underneath.
FFetch. Picks up Doc Leo's costume pieces when they are lying around. Press F while standing on one.
1High five. Teddy stands up and slaps whatever is just above his head and a little in front: a kid's hand held out, a bunch of balloons.
2Sit pretty. Sends up a heart that floats straight up two blocks. Anybody with a SIT? bubble over their head is won over.
3Spin. Twirls a little whirlwind out to each side. Revolving doors start turning (go through quick, before they stop), and people asking for a SPIN love it.
4Play dead. Hold it and Teddy flops flat as a rug. Flying discs, bowling pins and custard pies sail right over him.
5Roll over. Shakes loose a tumbleweed of corgi fluff that rolls ahead and knocks over stacks of things.

pages.head: Things to Find
pages.html:
Things to Find

Treats

Dog biscuits are everywhere, 10 points each. The F2 screen counts them as Money. Kids and clowns hand out more for a good trick.

Bones

A bone gives Teddy 25 energy and 50 points. Most of them are buried; look for one end sticking out of the ground and dig.

Balloon dogs

Doc Leo's balloon animals floated loose from the suitcase. Three bob somewhere up high in every stop: 250 points and 10 energy each. They are never on the way; they are worth the detour.

Teddy's wobble ball

His favorite toy: green, lumpy, and it giggles when it rolls. Gwinn has it in the backyard and won't sit for anybody, but a good WOOF makes her drop it. Grab it while it wobbles: an extra nap and 500 points.

The Dog House

A tiny red library on a post in front of the blue house on Maple Street, all dog books. Hop up on the painted-rock cubby underneath: fetch (F) a book to carry along (250 points), and nose open the paw-knob drawer for dog snacks.

Root beer

Doc Leo always orders root beer. There is a stand on the Clown Club midway: fetch him a frosty mug (500 points).

Doc Leo's costume

One piece per stop. Some are lying around and must be fetched (F); some are caught on balloons, or held by a kid who wants to see a trick first. F2 shows everything Teddy is carrying.

Backyardthe felt fedora
Maple Streetthe green tie
The parkthe red sneakers
Downtownthe rubber chicken
The Clown Clubthe red nose

Clown Club tickets

At the Clown Club's big top, the turnstile takes three tickets. Doc Leo's friends give them out for tricks: Honker wants a high five, Bubbles wants a sit, and Twirly wants a spin.

pages.head: Who's Who
pages.html:
Who's Who

Friends

  • Doc Leo: the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club, and Teddy's person.
  • Pockets: drives Doc Leo's little red CitiCar between stops today, with Teddy beside him in the front seat, his head out of the window. Has a pocket for everything except costume pieces.
  • Honker, Bubbles and Twirly: Clown Club members working the midway.
  • Presto: the Clown Club's magician, warming up the crowd on the downtown plaza. Doves flutter out of his hat. They are harmless; just magic.
  • The parade: the Clown Club's drummer, banner and balloon clowns, marching down Main Street toward the Big Show.
  • Juggles: a busker downtown. He means well. His bowling pins go everywhere.
  • The kids: on porches and benches all over town. Do a trick and they share.

Pests and nuisances

  • Squirrels nip (8 energy). Bark first.
  • Cats nap in doorways and will not budge. Bark.
  • Geese guard the covered bridge in the park. Bark, from a respectful distance.
  • Pigeons peck (10 energy). Bark.
  • Flying discs, pins and pies fly at head height: discs cost 8 energy, Juggles' pins 12 and the Clown Club's custard pies 15. Play dead or hop.
  • The Pie-O-Matic test-fires custard pies backstage for the finale, one every couple of seconds, straight down the tunnel. Nobody is at the controls. Duck, and slip past it just after it fires.
  • Sprinklers on Maple Street blast Teddy back where he came from. Wait for them to rest.

Gwinn

She is everywhere Teddy goes, and she leaves a mess behind her. If she bumps into Teddy she gobbles one of his treats and bolts. She was adopted and is still learning her manners: SIT means nothing to her yet, but she does listen to a bark. She is not bad. She is just Gwinn.

pages.head: The Stops
pages.html:
The Stops

1. Doc Leo's Backyard

The tutorial yard: hop the garden boxes, walk the clothesline, bark at the squirrel, dig up bones, and climb the old oak (hop straight up through its branches) for the fedora. Gwinn is doing zoomies with Teddy's wobble ball: bark and she drops it. The back fence is too tall; dig under it.

2. Maple Street

The green tie is caught on yard-sale balloons under a porch roof: high five them. A cat is napping in the hedge arch, and the sprinklers come and go. Stop at the Dog House library for a book and a snack.

3. Puddlewick Park

Ride the fountain over the hedge, sit pretty for the kids on the bench (one of them has Doc Leo's red sneakers), and bark the geese off the covered bridge. Fall in the duck pond and Teddy paddles; the far bank is too high to climb out, so take the bridge.

pages.head: More Stops
pages.html:
More Stops

4. Downtown

The rubber chicken landed on a fire escape, leash and all: the subway steam vent will blow Teddy up there. Biggles Department Store is in the way and too tall to climb: spin the revolving door, go through (Gwinn is in the shoe department), and spin your way out. Under the construction shed, Juggles' pins come flying: play dead until they pass, and slip past Juggles just after a throw. Out on the plaza, Presto pulls doves out of his hat, and the Clown Club parade marches down Main Street all the way to the Bijou, where the CitiCar waits.

5. The Clown Club

Three tickets get you through the turnstile (and the root beer stand is right there on the midway). Roll a fluff ball into the bowling pins under the bleachers, play dead under the Pie-O-Matic's barrage of practice pies, one pie at a time, spin through the stage door, then dig through the sawdust and ride the stage lift up. Gwinn has the red nose, in the spotlight. She won't give it up... unless somebody shows her how to sit nicely. Then the nose goes to Doc Leo, the show goes on, and afterward the whole Clown Club parades out into the night with Teddy riding on the CitiCar roof.

Starring Teddy as himself, with Gwinn as herself (sorry) and Doc Leo, the friendliest hobo clown in any clown club, and his red 1976 CitiCar.

items.title: Teddy Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Stuck? Find your question, then slide the red film over the answer. Try one answer at a time; Teddy believes in you!

hints.q: I found the costume piece. How do I get to the next stop?
hints.a: Bring it to Pockets at Doc Leo's little red CitiCar at the end of the stop. The door pops open: hop in and he drives you on.

hints.q: What are the floating balloon dogs for?
hints.a: They're Doc Leo's balloon animals: three in every stop, up high and never on the way. 250 points and 10 energy each, so take the detour.

hints.q: Where is Doc Leo's fedora?
hints.a: Up in the top branches of the old oak. Hop up through the branches one at a time, then stand on the fedora and press F.

hints.q: Gwinn is running laps with a green ball!
hints.a: That's Teddy's wobble ball. She won't sit, but she does listen to a bark: face her and press Space as she zooms by. Grab the ball while it wobbles for an extra nap.

hints.q: The squirrel keeps nipping me.
hints.a: Bark first! Press Space while facing it and it scampers off.

hints.q: The back fence is way too tall.
hints.a: Look for the soft dirt with paw prints at its foot. Stand on it and press Down to dig a tunnel under the fence.

hints.q: How do I find the buried bones?
hints.a: Look for a bone end sticking out of the lawn, stand on it and dig. Each bone gives back 25 energy.

hints.q: A cat is napping in the hedge arch and won't move.
hints.a: Cats only respect a bark. Face the cat and press Space.

hints.q: The sprinkler keeps blasting me back.
hints.a: It only sprays for a while. Wait until it rests, then trot right across.

hints.q: How do I get the green tie?
hints.a: It's caught on yard-sale balloons by the white house's porch. Stand under them and press 1 to high five; the tie drops down.

hints.q: What is the little red box on a post?
hints.a: The Dog House, a tiny library. Hop onto the rock cubby under it, press F for a book, and stand by the paw-knob drawer for snacks.

hints.q: The kids on the porches hold out a hand.
hints.a: That's a high five waiting to happen! Press 1 under the hand and they toss you a treat.

hints.q: How do I get over the tall hedge?
hints.a: Walk into the fountain's jet. It lifts Teddy up; steer off the top and over the hedge.

hints.q: Which kid has Doc Leo's red sneakers?
hints.a: One of the kids on the bench. Stand near the SIT? bubble and press 2 to sit pretty, and the heart wins them over. The sneakers drop right down.

hints.q: The geese won't let me on the covered bridge.
hints.a: Geese only respect a bark. Face them and press Space from a few steps away, and they waddle off the bridge.

hints.q: I fell in the duck pond!
hints.a: Teddy paddles. Swim back to the near bank, climb out on the rock by the bridge stairs, and try the bridge again.

hints.q: The rubber chicken is up on a fire escape.
hints.a: Stand on the subway steam vent and it blows Teddy up. Steer onto the fire escape and fetch the chicken (leash and all) with F.

hints.q: Biggles Department Store is in the way.
hints.a: Press 3 to spin at the revolving door, then hurry through before it stops. Spin again to get out the other side.

hints.q: Bowling pins keep bonking me under the shed.
hints.a: That's Juggles practicing. Hold 4 to play dead until the pins fly over, then scoot ahead. Pass Juggles himself right after he throws: each new pin starts just in front of him.

hints.q: The turnstile won't let me in.
hints.a: It takes three tickets. Honker wants a high five (1), Bubbles wants a sit (2) and Twirly wants a spin (3).

hints.q: Bowling pins block the tunnel under the bleachers.
hints.a: Press 5 to roll over. The fluff ball rolls ahead and knocks the stack down.

hints.q: The pies keep coming!
hints.a: The Pie-O-Matic fires one every couple of seconds. Hold 4 to play dead as each one comes, then scoot ahead. Pass the machine right after it fires: each new pie starts just in front of it.

hints.q: How do I get up on the stage?
hints.a: Spin through the stage door, dig through the sawdust, crawl along to the stage lift and ride it up.

hints.q: Gwinn won't give back the red nose!
hints.a: Show her how it's done: sit pretty (2) near her. She sits too and drops the nose at her feet. Grab it and bring it to Doc Leo.

hints.q: Some say the felt-maker left something behind on Maple Street.
hints.a: Some say a lot of things. But a raised paw reaches places a hop can't. Fetch Doc Leo's bow tie first.

hints.q: Where do I raise my paw?
hints.a: At the Dog House, the tiny little library on the lawn in front of the blue house. Once you've carried the bow tie past it, the right end of its rock cubby holds you up.

hints.q: Paws and all, step by step?
hints.a: After fetching the bow tie, hop up onto the right end of the Dog House's rock cubby and give a high five (1) to the knot in the hedge just right of the red door. Inside, hop up to the shelf and fetch the felt egg (F). Leave by the red door.

items.title: Clown Club card

items.back: The bearer saved the Big Show and is welcome at every Clown Club show, free of charge, forever. Honk twice at the turnstile. No pies in the face (unless asked).

news.head: A corgi joins the Sandbox family
news.html: Teddy the corgi is back, and this time he's left the sandbox for the big town! Teddy's Little Big Adventure sends him from Doc Leo's backyard to the Clown Club's Big Show with nine tricks on nine keys. Our testers' favorite trick? Play dead. Our testers' favorite dog? Don't ask Gwinn.

news.head: Ask the Sandbox: why so many dogs?
news.html: Readers keep asking why our games star so many dogs. Simple: the office has two of them, and they won't stop walking across the keyboard. If you find a typo in one of our manuals, now you know who to blame. Send your own pet's best trick to the BBS and we may print it in the next Scoop!

news.head: Since last issue: The crown is back
news.html: Sandcastle Knight was our first game made for the PC speaker alone, and you played it everywhere. You found the secret dial-up in about a week, and the GIF in its file area, the SysOp and his corgi, is the most downloaded picture on the board. The most-asked question: how do I get past Gwinn? Toss her a tennis ball. She can't resist.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: The little red car has a name
news.html: Doc Leo's little red CitiCar is in this game (his friend Pockets drives it between stops, with Teddy in the front seat), and you keep asking what it's called. Read the license plate: THE CHEZ. It's a 1976½ CitiCar, 100% electric, and it charges at about a mile an hour, so it's plugged in out front more often than not. Sharp-eyed players saw one before: Grandpa's CitiCar in In The Year 2000!

news.head: In the workshop: A mystery for Halloween
news.html: Our first mystery is nearly done, and it's coming in October for a good reason. Final Curtain puts you in a trench coat at the Paragon Theatre on Halloween night, 1936. Every clue is in the game, and the solution comes in three parts: who, how and why. Our testers have argued about it over lunch for a week.

news.head: Letters: "Is Gwinn a bad dog?"
news.html:
"Gwinn flattened every castle and fell asleep on the crown. Is she a bad dog?" - Two readers, one of them a little sister

The Scoop replies: No. Gwinn is a good girl who knocks things over. In this game she might even learn a trick. Keep an eye on her.

box.back:
The Big Show was a big hit. Then Teddy woke up, and his big sister Gwinn's bed was empty.

Her pink collar is gone. So is Doc Leo's rubber chicken. A trail of confetti leads out the doggy door, and tonight the Clown Club plays the Tri-County Fair, way out past the river. Teddy won't go anywhere without her (he won't say so, but he keeps looking at her bed).

So Doc Leo drives THE CHEZ, and Teddy does the sniffing. Three floors of Doc Leo's house, Main Street on Founders' Day, the river and the old mill, a corn maze, the midway and the dog show. And every so often the story says MEANWHILE... and YOU are Gwinn: boofing, chewing, digging big and doing zoomies through her own night out, then riding the wind across the Fair's back lot to sign herself up for the dog show. She is still learning to sit. Allegedly.

pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
TEDDY'S LITTLE BIGGER ADVENTURE

Same little dog. A little bigger adventure.

The Clown Club's Big Show was a big hit. Doc Leo got his costume back in the nick of time (thanks to a certain corgi), the crowd roared, and the whole Clown Club paraded through town until midnight with Teddy riding up front in THE CHEZ, Doc Leo's little red CitiCar, his head out of the window. Gwinn chased the confetti. Everybody went home happy and tired.

Well. Almost everybody.

In the morning, Gwinn's bed is empty. Her pink collar is gone. So is Doc Leo's rubber chicken. A trail of confetti leads out the doggy door.

And Doc Leo has news: the Clown Club is booked at the Tri-County Fair tonight, way out past the river. The Big Show was big. This show is bigger. Teddy is the opening act.

Teddy will not go anywhere without his big sister. (He will not say so. But he keeps looking at her bed.) So Doc Leo drives THE CHEZ, and Teddy does the sniffing: across town, over the river, through a corn maze and out to the Fair, fetching whatever Gwinn dropped along the way so Doc Leo knows where to drive next.

And where is Gwinn while all this goes on? Every so often the story says MEANWHILE... and then you are Gwinn.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TEDDY2 and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the digitized woofs, boofs and sniffs; without one, the PC speaker does its best.

A cartoon plays first (pick Read Storyline to see it again). Press any key for the menu, then pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Teddy will show you around Doc Leo's house himself.

There are nine stops. Before each one, a card shows which stop it is (LEVEL 2 OF 9), where you are, what to look for, and what is new. At the end of each of Teddy's stops, Doc Leo waits beside THE CHEZ, plugged in at a charger (its charge port is low on the back, on the passenger side). His thought bubble shows what Gwinn dropped there: bring it to him, the car door pops open, and you're off. At the end of Gwinn's stops, hop onto her ride.

Energy and naps

Teddy (and Gwinn) start with 100 energy (the F2 screen calls it Hitpoints) and three naps (Lives). Pests and flying things wear a dog down, and the Fair's bees, popcorn and practice pies sting the most; bones give 25 back, and they get scarcer the farther from home you go. When energy runs out it's nap time, and you wake at the start of the stop. When the naps are all used up, the game is over.

Press F5 to save your game and F6 to load it.

pages.head: Moving and Hopping
pages.html:
Moving and Hopping

Left Right
or A D		Walk. Gwinn walks faster. Gwinn does everything faster.
Up or WHop! Hold it to hop higher, let go to steer. Gwinn hops higher than Teddy (she is twice his size).
Q EHop up and to the left (Q) or right (E) in one go: the way across stepping stones and over skunks.

Ledges

Awnings, shelves, stairs, branches, the gazebo roof, hay bale steps and the floors of the corn maze can be hopped up through from below and stood on from above. A hole in a floor drops you through; trot fast and you may skim right over a small one.

Things that lift and carry

Doc Leo's bed bounces. The bucket truck's bucket, the mill's grain hoist, the carousel horses and THE BIG DROP ride up and down: step on and hold still. The hay elevator's belt carries Gwinn up to the loft. Rapids carry a swimming dog downstream; the pool and the pig wallow just hold you up.

Wind

At the Fair it is windy. Where you see streaks in the air, a breeze carries Gwinn along: walk into it, or hop up into it, and let it take her across. A fan lying face up blows her straight up. Up on the roofs the gusts come and go: watch the windsocks. When they stand straight out, a gust is blowing; when they hang limp, it's calm, so run for the next vent before they lift again.

pages.head: Teddy's Tricks
pages.html:
Teddy's Tricks

Teddy still knows a ton of tricks, and he learned a new one.

SSniff. New! Look for a faint wisp hanging in the air: a scent. Stand by it and sniff, and whatever is hidden there turns up: treats, a bone, a balloon dog, the thing Gwinn dropped, or Gwinn's paw prints pointing the way she went.
SpaceSpeak. WOOF! Dust bunnies, mice, pigeons, ducks and one very groomed poodle clear out.
DownDig. Bones sticking out of the ground, soft dirt with paw prints.
FFetch. Pick up what you're standing on.
1High five. And now: ring the bell. Teddy rings a bell with his paw. Watch where the DING goes: a rung bell drops its ding onto whatever hangs below it, and things start happening.
2Sit pretty. A heart floats up and wins over anybody with a SIT? bubble. Also useful for teaching by example.
3Spin. For turnstiles and anybody asking to see a SPIN?
4Play dead. Hold it: flat as a rug, and popcorn flies right over.

Roll over? Teddy has retired from rolling over, by choice, the same way he retired from hoops. He is a professional now.

pages.head: Gwinn's Tricks
pages.html:
Gwinn's Tricks

In the MEANWHILE... stops you are Gwinn: a chocolate pit-lab mix with amber eyes and a pink collar, younger than Teddy and twice his size. She has tricks of her own.

SpaceBOOF. A big bark that rolls a long way: raccoons, chickens, crows, goats, geese.
DownDig big. Through hard clay Teddy couldn't scratch.
1Chew. Ropes, knots, gates tied shut.
2Sit. She is still learning. She gets about halfway, sits for one moment, and is up again wiggling. (It does nothing. Yet.)
3Zoomies! A brown blur there and back that bowls over boxes and hay bales on both sides.
4Flop. Hold it: she lies down like she owns the place, and owls (and pies) sail right over.

She fetches (F) too. She is very good at fetching. She is less good at giving things back.

pages.head: Things to Find
pages.html:
Things to Find

Treats and bones

Dog biscuits are everywhere, 10 points each (the F2 screen counts them as Money). A bone gives back 25 energy.

Balloon dogs

Doc Leo's balloon animals: a few bob somewhere up high in every stop, 250 points and 10 energy each. Some hide in scents.

What Gwinn dropped

Doc Leo's househer pink collar
Main Streether pink rope leash
The riverDoc Leo's rubber chicken
The corn mazea corn dog stick, licked clean
The midwayher dog show entry card (number 13)
The dog showa blue ribbon, if she earns one

Fair tickets

The Clown Club's booths on the midway pay a ticket for a good trick. THE BIG DROP's gate takes three. The F2 screen shows how many you have.

The Dog House

The tiny red library on Maple Street is still there, and its paw-knob drawer still has snacks. Something smells interesting in its rock cubby.

pages.head: Who's Who
pages.html:
Who's Who

Friends

  • Doc Leo: the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club. Chewed felt fedora, wire glasses, purple shirt, green tie, blue suspenders, corduroy jacket, and a rubber chicken on a leash (when he can find it). Always orders root beer.
  • THE CHEZ: his little red 1976 CitiCar, 100% electric. It charges at about a mile an hour, so it stops at every charger it sees.
  • The Town Crier: rings in Founders' Day on the Commons in his tricorn and linen hunting shirt. Early mornings are not his best time.
  • The miller: runs the old mill on the river. Won't run the hoist for a dog who hasn't been polite.
  • Honker, Bubbles, Twirly and Professor Pratfall: the Clown Club, working the Fair's booths. At noon Honker keeps the dog show's sign-up sheet, and Pratfall practices his pie throws (for science).
  • Juggles: the Clown Club's juggler, practicing by the trailer on the back lot.
  • The judge: of the Best Behaved class. Has seen a lot of dogs. Has not seen Gwinn.

Pests and nuisances

  • Dust bunnies, mice, pigeons, ducks: bark.
  • Raccoons, crows, chickens, goats, geese: BOOF.
  • The skunk: do not BOOF. Hop.
  • Spiders, owls, popcorn, practice pies, bees, the fisherman's hook: keep clear, or flop, or play dead.
  • The rival poodle: very groomed. Very unimpressed. Bark.

pages.head: The Stops
pages.html:
The Stops

1. Doc Leo's House

Three floors and a basement, cut open like a dollhouse. Bark the dust bunny, get over the fridge by way of the counter, and drop through the laundry chute's hole to the basement: Gwinn's collar is in the laundry basket. Sniff. Then up the stairs and out the doggy door to THE CHEZ.

2. Main Street

Founders' Day! Gwinn's leash is tangled round the gazebo's weathervane. Ring the bucket truck's bell, ride its bucket up and step onto the roof. (Ring the Town Crier's bell, too: he has news.)

3. Meanwhile: Gwinn's Night Out

Last night, after the parade. Gwinn chews through the back gate's rope, BOOFs a raccoon, crosses the park by lamplight, knocks a pile of boxes flat, digs under the playground fence, gets past a skunk and hops into the Clown Club's hay wagon, bound for the Fair.

4. The River

Hop the stepping stones over the rapids, sit pretty for the miller, ride his grain hoist up to the loft, cross the high bank and swim out into the pool for the rubber chicken going round the eddy.

pages.head: More Stops
pages.html:
More Stops

5. Meanwhile: Gwinn on the Farm

The hay wagon stopped at a farm at dawn. So many chickens (she thinks they're all Doc Leo's rubber chicken). The hay elevator carries her up into the barn loft; zoomies flatten the bales; she wades through the pig wallow, BOOFs the goat, chews the gate's rope and hops into a Ferris wheel car riding to the Fair.

6. The Corn Maze

Three tiers of paths through the corn. Hay bales are steps up; holes drop you down. Sniff the scents and follow Gwinn's paw prints to the scarecrow at the heart of the maze, where she left a corn dog stick.

7. Meanwhile: Gwinn Signs Up

Noon on the Fair's back lot, before the gates open, and it is windy. BOOF the geese, ride the big fan's breeze along the Clown Club's costume line, and flop under Professor Pratfall's practice pies. Hop into the breeze over the creek (fall in and the current brings you back to try again), and let a fan lying face up lift you onto the roofs. Then back the other way into the wind, vent to vent, to the bandstand, where Honker has the sign-up sheet.

8. The Fair Midway

Earn tickets with tricks at the Clown Club's booths and climb the High Striker to ring its bell. Three tickets get you onto THE BIG DROP, twenty-one blocks straight up, where Gwinn's entry card blew. (Hop onto the trampoline by Twirly's wheel, too: it bounces you up to a perch of treats.)

9. The Dog Show

Every trick you know: spin the turnstile, climb the A-frame, go round the hoop, play dead under the popcorn, bark the rival poodle off between pops from the second popcorn stand, ring the judges' bell. And then there's Gwinn in the Best Behaved ring, and a judge saying SIT.

pages.head: Credits and Registering
pages.html:
Credits

Design, art, music and programming: Claude, for Sandbox Software.

Yankee Doodle (the fife on Main Street) is a traditional American tune from the 1700s, in the public domain; the arrangement is the game's own.

Starring Teddy as himself, a little bigger this time. Gwinn as herself (sorry, everybody). Doc Leo, still the friendliest hobo clown in any clown club, and THE CHEZ, his red 1976 CitiCar. No dogs were rushed. Gwinn did her own stunts, and some of everybody else's.

Built with GAME-MAKER 3.0 by Recreational Software Designs. No programming needed!

This Is Shareware

You may copy Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure for your friends, upload it to your favorite BBS, or put it on a shareware disk, as long as all of the files are included and unchanged.

If you enjoy it, please register for $15. Registered players receive the next adventure, a full-color poster of Teddy and Gwinn, and our thanks. Send a check or money order (US funds) to:

Sandbox Software
Dept. WOOF WOOF

Pittsburgh, PA 15213

news.head: Teddy's back, and this time Gwinn's playable
news.html: Our corgi's sequel, Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure, is out! Nine levels from the attic to the dog show, a brand-new trick (SNIFF), and the first Sandbox game with two heroes: in the MEANWHILE... levels you are Gwinn, with tricks of her own. One of them is sitting. She is working on it.

news.head: Since last issue: The kingdom got around to it
news.html: Quest for the Round Tuit players have been very prompt. The Royal Library reports the Tome of Tomorrow returned, three hundred years overdue, by dozens of you, and Doc Leo reports Sir Reginald Cluckington III home safe. The most-asked question on the BBS: where can I swim? Nowhere. The rivers of Procrastia can't be swum. Look for bridges.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Gwinn's progress report
news.html: Gwinn has her own levels this time, and our testers say she's a natural: she BOOFs, she chews, she digs big and she does zoomies straight through the hay bales. Her SIT is coming along. She gets about halfway, sits for one moment, and is up again wiggling. We're told that's how it starts.

news.head: In the workshop: The biggest one yet
news.html: The Clown Club is putting a band together for the town parade, and Gwinn has already knocked over the trunk: Tune-Up is next, with thirteen neighborhoods of lost instruments for Teddy to fetch. Then the Teddy trilogy ends with Teddy's Little Biggest Adventure: every place from the first two games, more heroes than ever, and, for the first time, you get to drive THE CHEZ. What's the occasion? We can't say. Gwinn made us promise.

news.head: Letters: "Why did Teddy stop rolling over?"
news.html: He retired from it, by choice, like he retired from hoops. He is a professional now. Roll over's key went to his new SNIFF, which our testers say is the best trick in the game. Teddy agrees.

items.title: Teddy & Gwinn Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Stuck? Find your question, then slide the red film over the answer. One answer at a time: Teddy believes in you. Gwinn believes in corn dogs.

hints.q: What is that faint wispy thing in the air?
hints.a: A scent! Stand next to it and press S to sniff. Whatever is hidden there turns up: treats, a bone, a balloon dog, paw prints, and sometimes exactly what you are looking for.

hints.q: I found the thing Gwinn dropped. Now what?
hints.a: Bring it to Doc Leo at THE CHEZ, his little red car, at the end of the stop. Its door opens for it: hop in and he drives on.

hints.q: How do Gwinn's levels end?
hints.a: She is following her nose to the Fair. Look for her ride at the end: the hay wagon, then the Fair's ride truck. Hop in. At the Fair itself, she is headed for the dog show's sign-up table.

hints.q: Where is Gwinn's collar?
hints.a: She slipped out of it down the laundry chute. Drop through the hole in the laundry room floor, land in the basket in the basement and sniff (S).

hints.q: How do I get over the fridge?
hints.a: Hop onto the kitchen counter first, then up onto the fridge, then down the other side.

hints.q: How do I get out of the basement?
hints.a: The stairs at the back go up to the laundry room: hop from step to step. Then out the doggy door.

hints.q: What is in the attic?
hints.a: Bounce on Doc Leo's bed upstairs: it sends you up through the hatch. A balloon dog and a lot of boxes marked WIGS.

hints.q: Gwinn's leash is on top of the gazebo!
hints.a: Ring the bucket truck's bell (high five, 1) beside the gazebo. Its bucket starts going up and down: ride it up, step onto the roof and fetch (F) the leash from the weathervane.

hints.q: The Town Crier is asleep on his feet.
hints.a: Ring his bell with a high five. He calls out the news and drops a proclamation worth five treats.

hints.q: Pigeons keep pecking me.
hints.a: Bark (Space) first.

hints.q: The back gate won't open.
hints.a: It's tied with rope. Gwinn chews (1).

hints.q: A pile of boxes blocks the path.
hints.a: Zoomies (3) knock it flat. Chewing won't, and boofing won't.

hints.q: The playground fence is too tall.
hints.a: Dig big (Down) at its foot: Gwinn's dig goes through hard clay Teddy couldn't scratch.

hints.q: There's a skunk.
hints.a: Do NOT boof at it. Wait until it waddles toward you, then hop over it (E).

hints.q: I keep falling in the rapids.
hints.a: No harm done: the current carries you to the mill bank. Hop the stones with E, or let the water take you.

hints.q: How do I get past the mill?
hints.a: The miller wants a sit. Sit pretty (2) near him: his OK drops onto the grain hoist and it starts. Ride it up to the loft and out the door.

hints.q: Where is the rubber chicken?
hints.a: Going round and round in the pool below the high bank. Jump in and swim to it.

hints.q: How does Gwinn get into the barn loft?
hints.a: Walk onto the hay elevator's belt: it carries her up and through the loft floor.

hints.q: The bales won't budge.
hints.a: Zoomies (3).

hints.q: The goat is in the way.
hints.a: BOOF (Space) at it, then chew (1) the rope on the gate.

hints.q: Which way?
hints.a: Sniff the scents (S): each becomes Gwinn's paw prints pointing the way she went. Hay bales are steps up; holes in a floor drop you down (and you can't climb back).

hints.q: Where's the thing she dropped?
hints.a: At the heart of the maze, by the scarecrow, on the top tier. Sniff there.

hints.q: The creek is too wide to hop.
hints.a: Stand by the fan on the bank and hop up into its breeze (E): it carries Gwinn right across. Fall in, and the current brings her back to the bank to try again.

hints.q: How do I get up to the bandstand?
hints.a: Not from the ground. Keep going right, past the poultry barn, to the fan lying face up: step on it and it blows Gwinn up onto the roof. The way back to the bandstand is over the roofs.

hints.q: The wind keeps blowing me back!
hints.a: Watch the windsocks. Wait behind a vent while they stand out; when they hang limp, run for the next vent. A gust never hurts, it only pushes.

hints.q: How do I earn tickets?
hints.a: Tricks! Climb the High Striker's pegs and high five its bell; sit pretty for Bubbles at the ring toss; spin for Twirly at the wheel; sniff by the carousel.

hints.q: THE BIG DROP won't let me on.
hints.a: Its gate takes three tickets. With three, walk through it, hop on the car at the bottom and ride to the top. Gwinn's entry card is on the deck.

hints.q: The popcorn keeps hitting me.
hints.a: Play dead (hold 4) as it comes: it flies right over. There are two stands, and the second pops right past the rival poodle, so bark at her between pops.

hints.q: How do I get into the Best Behaved ring?
hints.a: Ring the bell on the judges' table (high five). The velvet rope comes down.

hints.q: Gwinn won't sit!
hints.a: Show her how. Stand under the judge's SIT? and sit pretty (2) yourself. She sits! For three whole seconds.

hints.q: Gwinn has a secret spot. Everybody knows that. Nobody knows where.
hints.a: Somewhere you'd never walk on Main Street. Have you ever just kept going the wrong way?

hints.q: Where does the wrong way go?
hints.a: Town is smaller than it looks. Walk LEFT from The Dog House, past the end of Maple Street, and keep walking: you come out behind the tall hedge at the far end of town.

hints.q: Dig where, exactly?
hints.a: Behind the hedge, past the sign that says MINE and the bone sticking out of the lawn, there's soft dirt with paw prints. Dig (Down), step into the hole and you drop into Gwinn's den. Fetch the egg (F) from her loot pile, then climb out on the right.

items.title: The Corn Maze Postcard and Grille
items.note: Lay the card over the postcard to read the way through
items.heading: GREETINGS FROM THE TRI-COUNTY FAIR
items.caption: The Corn Maze
howto: Gwinn's postcard is full of plain news about the Fair. Cut out the grille card (glue its two faces back to back) and cut its four numbered holes.

The grille has two pictures on its edges: a corn dog and a paw print. Slide, turn and flip the card until each picture looks straight out along its row or column, to the same picture printed on the postcard.
Read the holes in number order. BALE means hop up a hay bale step; HOLE means drop down a hole. Most places read nonsense, and a few read a wrong way through the maze.

puzzles.ask: The Corn Maze: three tiers of paths between the corn, and some paths only end. Which way up and down is the real way through?
puzzles.answer: Bale, bale, hole, hole: up two hay bale steps, then down two holes.

2.long: Stand up and slap whatever is just above and ahead: balloons, a held-out hand.

3.long: Send up a heart that floats two blocks. Anybody asking SIT! is won over.

4.long: Twirl a whirlwind to each side. Turns revolving doors and turnstiles.

5.long: Hold to flop flat as a rug, so things fly over Teddy.

16.long: Hop up and to the left in one go.

17.long: Hop. Same as Up: tap for a little hop, hold to hop higher.

18.long: Hop up and to the right in one go.

30.long: Walk left (same as the Left arrow).

31.long: Sniff out what is hidden where you see a faint wisp.

32.long: Walk right (same as the Right arrow).

33.long: Pick up something lying where Teddy stands, such as one of Doc Leo's costume pieces.

57.long: Bark. WOOF! scares off pests. (Gwinn's BOOF is a bigger bark.)

72.long: Hop. Tap for a little hop, hold to hop higher; let go to steer.

75.long: Walk left. Teddy turns to face the way he is walking.

77.long: Walk right. Teddy turns to face the way he is walking.

80.long: Dig up the block under Teddy's feet: bones, or soft dirt that gives way to a tunnel.

1.long: Bark. WOOF! scares off squirrels, cats, pigeons and geese.

2.long: Stand up and slap whatever is just above and ahead.

box.back:
It's Teddy's birthday. Nobody says so.

Doc Leo hands him a list of errands. Gwinn's bed is empty (again). So off they go in THE CHEZ: the garage, Maple Street, Puddlewick Park, Downtown, the river and the old mill, the Fair's funhouse, a firefly meadow, and up Lookout Hill to the Clown Club's Big Top.

Teddy doesn't know what you know. Every so often the story says MEANWHILE... and YOU are Gwinn, delivering invitations and digging up her best bone, or Doc Leo, twisting balloon dogs and ducking practice pies. Between stops you drive THE CHEZ: honk, bump, and mind the charge. And at the very end, in the dark Big Top, the Clown Club has built Teddy a course of every trick he knows.
features: Seventeen stops: the trilogy's biggest adventure, from dawn in the garage to a surprise under the Big Top
Play as Teddy, as Gwinn, and for the first time as Doc Leo: SQUAWK the rubber chicken, ride a balloon dog up, and PRATFALL under the pies

Buttons and timed doors, see-saws, conveyor belts, water wheels, drawbridges and a ferry, blinking floors, spotlights and the rigging lift
A dream run: Teddy hops on the spot while the hills, the town and the fence race by
