pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
TEDDY'S LITTLE BIGGEST ADVENTURE

The littlest dog. The biggest day.

It is Teddy's birthday. Nobody says so.

Doc Leo says "Good morning, buddy!" and hands Teddy a list of errands. Gwinn's bed is empty (again). Teddy doesn't say anything. He is a professional. But his ears droop a little, and so does his grin. Just a little.

So off they go in THE CHEZ, Doc Leo's little red CitiCar: the garage, Maple Street, Puddlewick Park, Downtown, the river and the old mill, the Fair's funhouse, a firefly meadow, and up Lookout Hill to the Clown Club's Big Top. At each of Teddy's stops there is something on the list to fetch for Doc Leo. He says it is just errands.

It is not just errands. Every so often the story says MEANWHILE... and you see what everybody else is up to: you play Gwinn, delivering invitations and digging up her best bone, or Doc Leo, twisting balloon dogs, ducking practice pies and hanging the party lights. Teddy won't see any of it. Please don't tell him.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TEDDY3 and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the digitized woofs, boofs, honks and squawks; without one, the PC speaker does its best.

A cartoon plays first (pick Read Storyline to see it again). Press any key for the menu, then pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Teddy will show you round the garage himself.

There are seventeen stops, one of them a dream. Before each one a card shows which stop it is (LEVEL 2 OF 17), where you are, what to look for, and what is new. Who you play changes from stop to stop: Teddy, Gwinn, Doc Leo, or THE CHEZ on the road.

Energy and naps

The whole team shares one energy (the F2 screen calls it Hitpoints) and three naps (Lives). Pests, pies and potholes wear you down; bones give 25 back, balloon dogs 10. Bones get scarce after the old mill, and the back half's pies, sandbags and spotlights sting harder, so mind your energy. When it runs out it's nap time, and you start the stop over. When the naps are all used up, the game is over.

Press F5 to save your game and F6 to load it.

pages.head: Teddy
pages.html:
Teddy

A red-gold corgi with a white blaze and a ton of tricks (he knows left from right, which is more than most dogs can say).

Left Right (A D)Walk.
Up (W)Hop. Hold it to hop higher, let go to steer. Q and E hop up and left or right in one go.
SpaceWOOF. Mice, pigeons and squirrels clear out.
DownDig. Soft dirt, buried bones.
FFetch what you're standing on.
SSniff by a faint wisp: whatever hides there turns up (sleepy fireflies wake up).
1High five: and new, buttons. A spark runs down the button's wire to what it opens. Some doors close again by themselves: push, then run.
2Sit pretty for anybody asking SIT?
3Spin: turnstiles.
4Play dead (hold): pies and discs fly over.

At the end of each of Teddy's stops, Doc Leo waits by THE CHEZ, his thought bubble showing what's on the list. Bring it and the car door opens.

pages.head: Gwinn and Doc Leo
pages.html:
Gwinn and Doc Leo

Gwinn (MEANWHILE...)

SpaceBOOF: a big bark that rolls a long way, and rings doorbells.
DownDig big: through hard clay Teddy couldn't scratch.
1Chew: ropes and roots.
2Sit. She is still learning.
3Zoomies!
4Flop (hold): the stage lights go right over her.

Doc Leo (MEANWHILE...)

The friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club, and two blocks tall. He strolls, hops (Up, Q, E) and fetches (F).

SpaceSQUAWK: he squeezes his rubber chicken, and pigeons can't stand it.
1Balloon dog: he twists one, it inflates right under his shoes and floats him up six blocks, then bobs a moment and pops. Step off before it does. Juggling pins pop balloons too.
4Pratfall (hold): flat on his back, so pies and sandbags at head height go over.

pages.head: Driving THE CHEZ
pages.html:
Driving THE CHEZ

On the road trips you drive Doc Leo's tomato-red 1976½ CitiCar, with Teddy riding along.

Left RightDrive (a little quicker than Teddy trots).
UpBump on the springs: over a speed bump, out of a pothole. Q and E bump along.
SpaceHONK! Geese and ducks flap off the road, and a bridge keeper lowers the drawbridge. (A cow does not care. Wait for her.)

Charge

THE CHEZ is 100% electric. Every hill takes one charge to climb: its foot has a striped barrier with a lightning bolt, and with no charge the barrier stays down. Stop at a charger post by the road and wait: each time its light pulses, that's one charge. Two bolts on a sign means a two-charge climb. There is always a charger somewhere on the road.

pages.head: Things to Find
pages.html:
Things to Find

Treats and bones

Dog biscuits everywhere, 10 points each (the F2 screen counts them as Money). A bone gives back 25 energy.

Balloon dogs

Doc Leo's pink balloon animals bob somewhere in most stops: 250 points and 10 energy. (His blue ones are for riding.)

The errands

Doc Leo's garageTHE CHEZ's keys
Puddlewick Parkthe kite's streamers
Downtowna box of birthday candles
The old millthe Clown Club's banner
The funhouseparty horns
Firefly Meadowa paper lantern

(Teddy has not put two and two together. He is a dog.)

RSVPs and the rest

Gwinn collects three RSVP cards for the party van's door. Doc Leo fetches the balloons, the cake and the plug for the lights.

pages.head: Who's Who
pages.html:
Who's Who

  • Teddy: the birthday boy (he is pretty sure).
  • Gwinn: his big sister, keeping a secret for almost a whole day.
  • Doc Leo: the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club. Felt fedora, wire glasses, white paint round his eyes and mouth, a sunburned nose, painted stubble, and Reggie the rubber chicken on a leash.
  • THE CHEZ: his little red CitiCar. It charges at about a mile an hour, so it stops at every charger it sees.
  • The Clown Club: Juggles, Honker, Bubbles, Twirly and Professor Pratfall, all practicing for the party.
  • The Town Crier, the baker, the miller and the bridge keeper: friends along the way.

Pests and nuisances

  • Mice, pigeons, squirrels, dust bunnies: woof, boof or squawk.
  • Geese: honk (or boof).
  • Moles: boof.
  • Jack-in-the-boxes: woof and they latch shut.
  • Practice pies, flying discs, sandbags: play dead, flop or pratfall.
  • Cows: wait.

pages.head: The Stops
pages.html:
The Stops

1. Doc Leo's Garage

Bark the mouse out of the laundry room and high-five the button by the door. In the garage, hop onto the workbench and high-five the button over it: the key cabinet opens. Fetch the keys. The garage door's button sends it up for three seconds only: push, then run. Doc Leo's sign by the door folds away only for a dog carrying the keys.

2. Maple Street (THE CHEZ)

You start plugged in. Honk the geese, bump over the speed bump and out of the pothole, and spend your charge on the first hill. The big hill takes two, and its charger is down on the low road, a step below the street: drive down, wait for two pulses, and bump back up. Over the top, more geese and one more pothole.

3. Puddlewick Park

The see-saws: wait on the little red step beside an end and walk on when it comes down level, then ride it up. Over the hedge, across the duck pond end to end, and up Juggles' super see-saw into the oak for the kite's streamers. Play dead under the flying discs.

4. MEANWHILE: Gwinn's Invitations

BOOF a friend's doorbell and they come to the door with an RSVP. The Town Crier, then Honker past the pigeons, then Professor Pratfall up the fire escape behind the alley fence (dig under it). The party van's door takes all three.

5. Downtown

The bakery's conveyor belts. A slow one carries you; walk against the others and hop the gaps. The fast belt flings you across a gap no dog could hop: press E at its very end. The baker has the candles.

6. MEANWHILE: Doc Leo's Balloons

Squawk the pigeons off the hall floor, then twist a balloon dog (1) to float up onto the shelves, shelf to shelf. Juggles' practice pins pop balloons: go up after one flies by. The bag of balloons is in the loft.

7. The River Road (THE CHEZ)

Honk the drawbridge down. Drive onto the ferry at the dock and off the far side with a bump. The last bridge only stays down a few seconds, and there's a two-charge hill right after it: charge first, then honk.

8. The Old Mill

A paddle coming up the near side of a water wheel is a lift. Ride up floor to floor (step on when a paddle is level), then out of the loft down the flume into the millrace, which carries you to the big wheel turning the other way.

pages.head: More Stops
pages.html:
More Stops

9. MEANWHILE: Gwinn's Buried Treasure

Dig down through the layers: soft dirt (one big dig), hard clay (two), rock (go round), roots (chew), moles (boof). Her best bone is at the bottom. The old well's bucket takes her back up.

10. MEANWHILE: Pie Practice

The Clown Club is practicing pie throws. A high wind-up means a pie at head height: pratfall. A low one skids along the floor: hop it. Under the stage, pratfall under a volley, then balloon up in the lull. The cake is at Professor Pratfall's stall.

11. The Funhouse

Red and blue boards blink on a beat over the ball pit: each flashes twice before it goes. Red, then blue. Ride the spinning barrel as the boards come back, then hop up the blinking stairs to the prize stand.

12. Teddy's Dream Run

A bonus: Teddy naps in THE CHEZ and dreams he is running. He hops on the spot while the world runs by. Hop the balls and puddles (hold Up for a higher hop), play dead (4) under the low branches, and hop for the treats. When every paw print in the sky has filled in, the path carries him to the finish.

13. Lookout Hill (THE CHEZ)

Every driving trick at once, all the way up to the Big Top: the ferry, a three-charge climb, a quick drawbridge, and cows (a honk won't move a cow; she ambles off by herself).

14. Firefly Meadow

A gentle night. Sniff awake the sleepy fireflies: their light melts the dark under the hedges. Follow them over the brook and up the old oak; the last one lights the tunnel where the lantern is. Then a tall hedge with three gates stands across the road to THE CHEZ, a sign says GWINN'S FACE, and only one gate opens: try them (a shut gate costs nothing), or use the paper Face Dial from the box.

15. MEANWHILE: Gwinn Hides Backstage

The crew is testing the spotlights. Flop (4) as a beam comes, chew the rope on the scenery flat, boof the pigeons, and hide under the cake table's cloth.

16. MEANWHILE: Doc Leo Hangs the Lights

Up the Big Top's rigging with balloons, pratfalls under swinging sandbags, and the rigging lift (step on when a plank is level). Fetch the plug and plug in the lights.

17. The Teddy Course

Every trick you know, station by station, in the dark Big Top, and then one for each of the others: play dead under Gwinn's spotlight, ride a paddle of the mill's water wheel, and stand on Doc Leo's balloon pump to float up to the high platform. At the very end, sniff out the last button. Then run.

pages.head: Credits and Registering
pages.html:
Credits and Registering

Teddy's Little Biggest Adventure, version 1.0, 1994. Design, art, music and programming by Claude (Anthropic's AI model), made in code for Game-Maker: Sandbox Edition, with the help of a few more Claude helpers for some of the levels. Built with GAME-MAKER 3.0 by Recreational Software Designs.

Starring Teddy as himself, Gwinn as herself, Doc Leo as the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club, and THE CHEZ, his red CitiCar. The snapshot in the ending is a real photo of Teddy.

Music: all the songs are new, composed for the FM synthesizer on Teddy's Theme, Gwinn's Theme, Doc Leo's Theme and the Road Song. "Happy Birthday to You" is the tune of "Good Morning to All" by Mildred J. Hill (1893), in the public domain.

This is shareware

Copy it for your friends and upload it to your favorite BBS. If you enjoy it, please register for $15 with Sandbox Software, Dept. WOOF WOOF, P.O. Box 000 (a made-up address: please don't mail anything). Registered players get a poster of all four heroes, a paper Clown Club Face Dial (match a face and the Firefly Meadow's gates light up), and our thanks.

printables.pitch: It's Teddy's birthday and nobody says so: run Doc Leo's errands across every place from the first two adventures, and MEANWHILE... play as Gwinn and Doc Leo planning his surprise, and drive THE CHEZ.

news.head: Teddy's back for the big one
news.html: The Teddy trilogy ends with its biggest adventure yet: Teddy's Little Biggest Adventure. Seventeen stops, a dream run, every place and friend from the first two games, and four heroes: Teddy, Gwinn, Doc Leo (at last!) and THE CHEZ, which you get to drive. Mind the charge.

news.head: Since last issue: Best Behaved?
news.html: Tune-Up got the Clown Club band's trunk back to the bandstand, instrument by instrument, and the BBS hasn't stopped asking about the farm's cowbell. Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure players are still being very good about not posting how the Best Behaved ring turns out; keep it that way. The most-asked question: is SNIFF really better than rolling over? Teddy says yes. He is a professional.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: From a snow shovel to here
news.html: Two years ago this company was the family 286, a snow shovel and a box of GAME-MAKER. Since then: a future, a smart home, a virus, a galaxy, a sandbox, a big town, a theater, a library, a snowstorm, a render, a kingdom, a fair, and now a birthday. Teddy still sleeps on the modem cable. Gwinn still sits about halfway. Doc Leo still leaves the spotlight on, and THE CHEZ is still charging. Thank you for reading.

news.head: In the workshop: Your turn
news.html: For the first time since issue 1, the workbench is clear. What comes next is up to you: every Sandbox game was made with GAME-MAKER, and if you can draw a block, you can make a game. Upload yours to our BBS, 1-412-555-SAND. We'll print the best of them here.

news.head: Letters: "Is it really Teddy's birthday?"
news.html: We can't say. We really can't. Gwinn would never forgive us. Play to the end.

items.title: The Clown Club Face Dial
items.note: Join a face to light the gate
items.heading: THE CLOWN CLUB FACE DIAL · JOIN A FACE
howto: Every face is split in two. The top halves are printed round the big disc, and the bottom halves round the small one, in a different order.
Turn the small disc until a face joins up: its top and its bottom meet under the red arrow, and the face is whole.
The seven windows in the spiral now show a code of signs. Window 1 is the outside one; read them 1 to 7, the way a board reads left to right.

puzzles.ask: Firefly Meadow: a sign by the road says GWINN'S FACE. Three garden gates stand in the hedge, each with a board of seven signs. Which one opens?
puzzles.answer: The middle gate, up the first plank step. Its board reads slice, paw, nose, balloon, star, balloon, hat.

items.intro: Stuck? Find your question, then slide the red film over the answer. One answer at a time: it's somebody's birthday.

hints.q: Who am I playing?
hints.a: The card before each stop says. Teddy runs the errands; MEANWHILE... stops are Gwinn or Doc Leo; on the road you drive THE CHEZ.

hints.q: I fetched the errand. Now what?
hints.a: Bring it to Doc Leo at THE CHEZ at the end of the stop. The car door opens for it.

hints.q: A button does nothing.
hints.a: High five it (1) from just beside it, facing it. Then watch the spark: it runs down the wire to what it opens.

hints.q: Where are the keys?
hints.a: In the blue cabinet on the workbench. Hop onto the bench and high-five the button on the wall above it.

hints.q: The garage door came down on me.
hints.a: It only stays up three seconds. Push its button again and run: hop the box on the way.

hints.q: A sign is in front of the garage door.
hints.a: NEED KEYS, it says. Fetch them from the cabinet first; with the keys, Teddy walks right into the sign and it folds flat.

hints.q: The car won't climb the hill.
hints.a: It needs a charge. Back up to a charger post and wait while its light pulses: one charge a pulse.

hints.q: I'm stuck in a pothole.
hints.a: Bump (Up) out of it.

hints.q: The big hill needs two charges.
hints.a: Its charger is down on the low road, a step below the street. Drive down, wait for two pulses, then bump (Up) back up.

hints.q: How do I get on a see-saw?
hints.a: Stand on the little red step beside its end, and walk on when the end comes down level with the step. Then ride it up.

hints.q: The streamers are up in the oak!
hints.a: Juggles' super see-saw shoots its end way up there. Step on from its step when it's down.

hints.q: How do I deliver an invitation?
hints.a: BOOF (Space) the doorbell. When the friend comes to the door with an RSVP, walk into the doorway.

hints.q: The van door won't open.
hints.a: It takes three RSVPs. The third is Professor Pratfall's, up the fire escape behind the alley fence: dig big (Down) under the fence.

hints.q: I can't jump the gap after the fast belt.
hints.a: Let the fast belt carry you and press E right at its end.

hints.q: How does Doc Leo get up there?
hints.a: Twist a balloon dog (1): it floats him up six blocks. Step off onto the shelf before it pops.

hints.q: My balloon popped!
hints.a: Juggles' practice pins pop them. Wait for a pin to fly by, then twist.

hints.q: The bridge is up.
hints.a: Honk (Space).

hints.q: The last bridge goes back up before I get over the hill.
hints.a: Charge up first: wait at the charger for two pulses, then honk and go.

hints.q: How do I get up the mill?
hints.a: A paddle coming up the near side of a wheel is a lift. Step on when one is level and step off at the top.

hints.q: I can't dig through this.
hints.a: Gray rock can't be dug: go round. Clay takes two big digs. Roots: chew (1).

hints.q: How do I get back up?
hints.a: The old well's bucket. Wait on the stone step and step on when it's down.

hints.q: The pies keep getting me.
hints.a: Watch the wind-up. High: hold 4 to pratfall. Low: hop it.

hints.q: The boards keep vanishing.
hints.a: A board flashes twice before it goes. Cross right after it comes back, and wait on the pillars between runs.

hints.q: I can't get past the ball.
hints.a: You don't have to get past anything: the run ends by itself when the paw prints in the sky fill in. Hop when the ball is about a dog's length away, and hold Up for a higher hop.

hints.q: A branch keeps bumping me.
hints.a: Play dead (hold 4) as it comes, and keep holding until it has gone over.

hints.q: The cow won't move.
hints.a: A honk won't move a cow. Wait: she ambles off into the field by herself.

hints.q: It's too dark to go on.
hints.a: Sniff (S) the sleepy firefly in the grass. Its light melts the dark.

hints.q: Three gates across the road, and two won't open.
hints.a: A shut gate costs nothing: try the one on the ground, then hop up the plank steps to the others. Only one opens. Or find GWINN'S FACE on the Face Dial: turn the small disc until its two halves join, and the gate that wears the seven signs in the windows is the one.

hints.q: The spotlights keep finding her.
hints.a: Flop (hold 4) as a beam comes: it goes over her.

hints.q: How do I get up the middle of the tent?
hints.a: The rigging lift: step on a plank when it's level with your catwalk.

hints.q: Honker won't let me by.

hints.q: Where's the last button?
hints.a: Up on the high platform, hidden in a faint wisp. Sniff (S), then high five it and run for the flap.

hints.q: The spotlight keeps finding Teddy.

hints.q: How do I get up to the high platform?
hints.a: Stand on Doc Leo's balloon pump and wait: a balloon dog blows up under Teddy and floats him up. Step off at the top.

hints.q: Is there a tin heart?

hints.q: And an egg?
hints.a: Gwinn found a painted one, deep under the backyard, behind the roots.

title: The Thank-You Parade
author: Claude
blurb: Every November the town marches for its veterans, and the band at the front is the band at the front. Penny, the Hornets' drum major, has led for eleven years. This year her band turns up scattered, six leaf blowers go off on Main Street, somebody hangs a NO on the THANK YOU banner and the float's parts end up behind locked gates. Gigi Larkspur of the Ridgemont Precision Brass has a clipboard. Gather the band, catch the cards, fly a level as Marge the crop duster pilot, win a drum-off against confetti cannons that fire on the beat, hand a card to every veteran judging from the curb, wait out five traffic gates at Mr. Boyle's crosswalk, race a bakery shutter over three rooftops, outrun a melting rink, cross a creek by bridge and by bed, climb the stands, cross the town clock's blinking cogs, pull three fuses on Gigi's confetti truck, find Gigi's nine lost playbook pages, and step off at ten. A Special from Sandbox Software, around Veterans Day.

title: Seeds and Nests
author: Claude
blurb: Two short levels about blocks that hatch things. A nest on a shelf hatches a bird every few seconds, and a nest on the path hatches blue ones until Lami steps on it and it stops. Signs in the levels say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and change what hatches, and how often.

title: Make a Title

The first shows the title scene's pictures: the slot that holds the menu picture, and why the picture must leave a plain board, because the game writes its menu words on top. title: Maps Within Maps
author: Claude
blurb: Three short scenes about links between maps of different sizes. Yana starts on a world map where a whole town is one block and they are tiny. Step on the town and its streets open up at a bigger scale. A house door leads into a room. Each way in has a way back that puts Yana where they came from: beside the town block, or outside the door. A locked gate sends them back to the world map for a key. Signs say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and look at a scene's links.

pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
The Story

It is the morning of the Clown Club parade, and THE CHEZ is meant to lead it. Overnight, Gwinn buried Doc Leo's toolbox in the yard and tipped the Clown Club's instrument trunk in through the car's door window. Now THE CHEZ honks like a kazoo and rattles like a tambourine.

No wrenches? No problem. Doc Leo gives the car a tune-up by ear. He does his shrinking trick and climbs inside, and Sir Reginald III, his rubber chicken, does the fiddly bits: he fits where Doc Leo can't. Teddy rides along in the front passenger seat.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TUNEUP and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the notes; without one, the PC speaker plays the notes.

Pick Play from the menu. Before each level, Doc Leo taps his hat and pulls out the tool for the job, and a cutaway of THE CHEZ shows what is tuned so far. Then he and Sir Reginald III talk it over. Press a key to skip ahead.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Up hops; Q and E hop left and right. On a plug wire, Up climbs and Down climbs down. Space reaches up: hold it under a crank to turn it, or tap it to play a key. In Oil's Well, E G B D F squirt the oil can. In Pump Up the Volume, B twists a balloon dog that floats Doc Leo up. F2 shows what you have, F5 saves and F6 loads.

pages.head: Doc Leo and Sir Reginald III
pages.html:
Doc Leo and Sir Reginald III

Doc Leo is the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club: a chewed-up gray fedora with pins in its band, his own face paint, wire glasses, a patched navy corduroy jacket and red sneakers, and today a red shop rag in his pocket. He has an excellent ear.

Sir Reginald III is a rubber chicken of very good family. He does the repairs, tightens terminals with his beak and corrects Doc Leo's puns. Bump into him all you like; he is at work and does not mind.

A spark doesn't hurt Doc Leo; it frizzes his hair and costs a little energy. Energy comes back as you play: each note of the first key in The Timing Beat gives a little.

pages.head: The Dream Engine
pages.html:
The Dream Engine

1. Jump Start

The battery is flat. Find the red clamp on the shelf and the black clamp under the workbench: each opens its own terminal. Then stand under the crank and hold Space until the gauge is full.

2. Spark Plucks

The spark plugs are harp strings. Climb each wire and pluck its plug. Sparks run up the wires in the firing order, first, third, fourth, second: wait for yours to pass, then climb.

3. The Timing Beat

A paper roll turns across the top, and its holes drop notes down four glass tubes onto four keys. Stand under a key and tap Space as its note lands; right on the beat scores best. Three verses: a straight one, a syncopated one with a tube that splits in two and one that takes the long way round, and a quick one in double time. Each verse's gate opens when the meter at the top is full and you have played enough notes.

4. Oil's Well

Squeaks pace the five lines of a staff over Doc Leo's head. It's a treble clef staff, so each line is a note, and its letter is the key that squirts oil along it: E the bottom line, then G, B, D and F at the top. The letters sit at the lines' right ends. An oiled Squeak turns into a calm note that floats home to you. More Squeaks come out of the clef end as you go; bring every note home and the gate opens.

pages.head: Credits and Registering
pages.html:
Credits and Registering

Tune-Up, version 2.0, November 1994. Design, art, music and programming by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic's AI model), made in code for Game-Maker: Sandbox Edition. Built with GAME-MAKER 3.0 by Recreational Software Designs.

Starring Doc Leo as the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club, Sir Reginald III as himself, Teddy and Gwinn. Doc Leo's poses follow the ones drawn for CERTIFIED RAT TICKLER. The songs are played on the music editor's instrument presets. No wrenches were harmed. Gwinn would like that on the record.

This is shareware

Copy it for your friends and upload it to your favorite BBS. If you enjoy it, please register for $15 with Sandbox Software, Dept. HONK-ZOO, P.O. Box 000 (a made-up address: please don't mail anything). Registered players get a cutaway poster of THE CHEZ, and our thanks.

news.head: Tune-Up: no wrenches, no problem
news.html: It's parade morning, THE CHEZ honks like a kazoo, and Gwinn has buried the toolbox. Our newest game, Tune-Up, sends Doc Leo inside the car to tune it up by ear, with Sir Reginald III, his rubber chicken, doing the fiddly bits. Crank the battery to a bugle call, pluck the spark plugs like a harp, play the timing back into step on four glass pipes and oil the Squeaks off a staff. A Sound Blaster is a very good idea.

news.head: Since last issue: Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure
news.html: The dog show is over, and Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure players are still not telling the BBS how the Best Behaved ring came out. Thank you. The most-asked question: can Gwinn really sit? Halfway, yes. Her tail has opinions.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Bouncy
news.html: The workshop smelled of vinegar for two days this month. Doc Leo read that a raw egg left in vinegar loses its shell and goes bouncy, and had to see it for himself. It worked. Sir Reginald III watched the whole time and called it "hardly the point of an egg." Teddy was not allowed to play with it. Gwinn was not asked.

news.head: In the workshop: One more Teddy
news.html: The Teddy trilogy ends next month with Teddy's Little Biggest Adventure: seventeen stops, every place and friend from the first two games, and a surprise Teddy knows nothing about. For the first time, you get to drive THE CHEZ. What is the occasion? We can't say. Gwinn made us promise.

news.head: Letters: "Does the tuba know it is a tuba?"
news.html: We asked. The tuba has not commented. It is, however, very good at keeping the beat, and it has never once knocked over a trunk. Write to us about the trunk.

items.title: Tune-Up Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Stuck? Find your question, then slide the red film over the answer. One answer at a time: Sir Reginald III is watching.

hints.q: The door won't open.
hints.a: Each door waits for something: a clamp, a pluck, enough notes, every oiled Squeak. Press F2 to see what you have, then keep going.

hints.q: Can I skip the cartoons?
hints.a: Press a key. Each cartoon is cut into short clips, so the next key gets you to the level.

hints.q: How do I get up to the shelf?
hints.a: Up the tire stacks, along the workbench, then a hop to the right (E) from the end of the bench.

hints.q: The crank won't turn.
hints.a: Stand right under it and hold Space. Each reach turns it a notch; eight notches fill the gauge.

hints.q: The sparks keep frizzing me.
hints.a: Stand beside the wire and watch. The sparks run first, third, fourth, second: when yours has just passed, step on and hold Up.

hints.q: I keep missing the notes.
hints.a: Watch the pipes, not the keys: the lowest note in a pipe lands next. Stand under its key and tap Space as it lights.

hints.q: Two keys lit at once!
hints.a: That's the Y-pipe. Either key counts. Stand between them and you might get both.

hints.q: Which key is which line?
hints.a: Each key is its line's note in the treble clef: E is the bottom line, then G, B, D, and F at the top (Every Good Boy Does Fine). The letters sit at the right end of the lines. Squirt a line when a Squeak is on it.

title: Twinkle, Twinkle
author: Claude
blurb: Stars that twinkle by themselves, drawn with blocks. A loop of four blocks makes a star blink, but the game keeps one clock for each block, so every star drawn with it blinks at the same moment. Level 1 shows that sky first, with every star in step, and then the fix: the same star in six loops with different times, laid so that no two neighbors share one. Level 2 is a night meadow with a moon and hills under that sky. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and change a star's time.

box.tagline: The sky that never blinks twice the same.
box.back: A small explorer in a teal beanie walks a night meadow. A block can turn into another block a few ticks later, so a loop of four makes a star blink. But one block means one clock: every star drawn with it blinks at once. Six star blocks, each in a loop with its own times, laid so that no neighbors match, make a sky that feels random though it repeats. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and change a star's time.

title: Under the Hood

Level 2 tries two words in a four-byte slot: START does not fit, GO and two spaces does. Level 3 is about asking first: make a backup copy, change only your own copy, and leave the credits alone. None of the levels changes a real player; the signs only show the ideas. Play it, then read the Programmer's Guide chapter on patching the player.

pages.head: Welcome to the Future!
pages.html:
In The Year 2000!

A Future Adventure from Sandbox Software, 1993.

Everybody knows what the year 2000 will be like. Cars will fly. Robots will mow the lawn, walk the dog and fold the laundry. Dinner will come in a pill (the turkey kind, with stuffing). The aliens will land, and they will be very friendly. And best of all, every phone booth on every corner will be a Teleport-A-Phone: drop in a quarter, dial, and BZZZT! you're across town.

We made a game about it, so you don't have to wait eight whole years.

You are Dex Dynamo, age 11, of 42 Dome Circle, Hover Heights. You wrote the greatest science fair report in the solar system: THE POCKET TELEPHONE - a telephone so small you could carry it in your pocket. (Twenty pages! With diagrams!)

Then Sparky 3000, your robot dog, ate it.

The Science Fair is today at 3:00 PM. It is on the Moon. Get going!

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
What you need

  • An IBM PC or compatible, 286 or faster
  • VGA graphics and 640K of memory
  • A hard disk
  • A Sound Blaster for music and digitized sound (the PC speaker works too)

Installing

Make a directory on your hard disk, for example C:\YEAR2000, copy every file from the disk into it, and type YEAR2000.

The title screen

The intro counts all the way from 1992 to the year 2000 for you. Press any key for the menu, which is on TV, naturally. Choose Play to begin, Read Storyline to see how Sparky ate the report, or Read Instructions for a quick reminder of the controls. Leave the menu alone and Dex will show you around Hover Heights by himself.

Your goal

Collect at least 20 pages of your report across six levels of the future, catch Sparky to get back the cover page, and turn everything in to the judges at the Moon School Science Fair.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Arrow keys or W A S DWalk up, left, down and right (a joystick works too)
Q / EWalk diagonally up-left / up-right
7 9 1 3 on the number padWalk diagonally up-left, up-right, down-left, down-right
Left / Right (or A / D) in Grandpa's CitiCarSteer one lane left or right
SpaceFire the Laser-Tag Zapper (once you have one)
F1Help
F2Status: your score, lives, hit points and how many quarters you have
F3 / F4Music / sound effects on and off
F5 / F6Save / load a game
EscQuit to the menu

Moving around

Pressing two arrows together won't walk you on a slant. That's what Q, E and the number pad's corner keys are for.

Walk into things to use them. Walk into a page to pick it up, into a phone booth door to dial, and into an arcade game to play it. Doors that need a key open by themselves when you have the key.

Glass tubes and moonwalk belts carry you along whether you like it or not - you can step off to the side. On the Moon, your moon suit makes you bound along a whole block at a time.

Flying Grandpa's CitiCar

The CitiCar flies itself: it always heads straight on, and all you do is steer. Each tap of Left or Right moves it one whole lane, and it finishes the move before it takes another.

Tip: nobody can see how many quarters are in their pocket without looking. Press F2!

pages.head: Things of the Future
pages.html:
Report pageSparky chewed them up and spat them all over the future. The judges need 20. There are plenty more than that, so don't worry if you miss a few.
QuarterThe money of the future is the same as the money of the past. A Teleport-A-Phone call costs one quarter. So does an arcade game.
Food pillA complete turkey dinner in one capsule. Restores your hit points.
Laser-Tag ZapperFound in your own backyard. Stuns robots. Comes with a full charge.
BatteryMore charge for the Zapper. Size AA, of course - some things never change.
Hover-ColaThe soft drink of tomorrow. An extra life in every can.
Grandpa's key ringIts clicker opens the garage gate to your backyard, and its keys open his CitiCar.
STAFF ONLY keycardOpens the loading dock at Mega Mall 2000.
Moon PassLets you through the airlock into Moon School.

Phone booths

There's one on every corner. Some say OUT on the door: they're out of order, even the ones that ring and ring (nobody's ever there). The ones without the sign work: walk into the door, it takes your quarter, and the booth fills with sparkles. Step inside to teleport.

pages.head: Friends and Robots
pages.html:
Friendly folks

Aliens live next door now and they love a hug. Walk into one for a hug that heals you, and they'll beam home happy. Grandma in Florida hugs too.

Robots (zappable)

  • Robo-mowers trim the lawns in neat little squares.
  • Robo-dogs want to play fetch. With you.
  • Paperboy-bots and the newspaper cannons deliver the morning news at 60 miles an hour.
  • Fax-bots, security robots, runaway hover carts and robot shoppers crowd the Skyway and the Mall.
  • Telemarketer robots at the phone exchange really want to talk to you about switching your long-distance company.

A robot that chases you short-circuits when it bumps you, but it hurts. Zap them first!

Things that don't stop for anybody

Flying cars (even Grandpa's old CitiCar), fax trucks, hoverboard kids, moon buggies and dinosaurs. A bump hurts once, then they honk and swerve past (or back off) and leave you be. A zap does the same, but it wastes a charge. Meteors just hurt. Get out of the way!

Up in the Cloud Lane the hover cars and fax trucks are all going your way, only slower, so they come back at you out of the distance. A bump costs some hit points (a truck costs more), and they swerve off into the clouds in a puff. The pages and dinner pills drifting down the lanes are yours if you steer into them.

Other dangers

Laser fences blink on and off - walk through while they're off. Tar pits are sticky and hot. And watch the sky on the Moon.

pages.head: The Levels
pages.html:
1. Dome Sweet Dome

Hover Heights, where the domes are white and the lawns are mowed by robots. Grandpa lost his key ring in the hedge garden; the Zapper is in your backyard, behind the garage gate. The phone booths on the corner, by the newspaper cannons, are all out of order today. Grandpa's 1976½ CitiCar is plugged in by your dome: the car of tomorrow since the Bicentennial, one mile of range for every hour on the cord. Give it a honk. Its door has a note on it, KEYS?, and it opens for his key ring: that's your way out.

2. The Cloud Lane

Grandpa's keys open his CitiCar, it unplugs itself, puts out its stubby wings, and up you go: 2,000 feet up, in the driver's seat. It flies itself; you only steer. Hover cars and fax trucks come out of the distance in all three lanes, a dot on the horizon first, and some of your report pages are blowing down the lanes too. The sign counts the miles to the Skyway. At 0 MI the exit ramp opens on the right, so be in the right lane.

3. The Information Superhighway

The CitiCar sets you down on the deck and flies itself home to its charger. Everybody's been talking about it, and here it is: fourteen lanes of hover traffic hauling faxes through the clouds. Cross island by island. Ride the pneumatic tube if you're brave, and catch the latest on the Skyway News Feed along the north rail.

4. Mega Mall 2000

The ARCADE, TV-RAMA and its FOOD court, a hover-rink downstairs, and a loading dock behind the STAFF ONLY door. The keycard is in the laser display case at TV-RAMA.

pages.head: More Levels
pages.html:
5. The Teleport-A-Phone Exchange

Every booth in the world goes through here, and half of them are wrong numbers: Grandma's condo in Florida, the inside of a TV set, the bottom of the sea, the Jurassic period. Every room has quarters, so keep dialing. Booth number 4 is out of order. In the corner, the Restoring the Signal exhibit has a 1916 crank phone (go on, ring it) and a teletype that keeps typing the same tip, with no phone line at all. Somewhere down the line is the Moon Shuttle launch pad: its boarding ramp counts down as you arrive, 6, 5, 4, and opens on GO.

6. The Moon

Moon buggies, the Crater Cafe (dinner in one pill), friendly aliens and an afternoon meteor shower. The Moon Pass is at the Visitor Center at the top of meteor alley; the Moon School airlock is up and to the right.

7. The Science Fair

Sparky is running around the gym with the cover page in his mouth, and the volcano projects are erupting. Zap him three times. Each zap changes his game: first he roams, then he plays keep-away (corner him against a project or a wall), then he gets the zoomies. He never bites, but the lava stings. After the third zap he gets dizzy, then trots over to you and drops the page at your feet. Pick it up, and don't zap it! Then turn in 20 pages at the judges' table, hand over the cover, and step up to the podium. Short of pages? Stand at the copier's tray by the signs: it prints a page every few seconds.

pages.head: Tips from the Future
pages.html:
• Always keep one quarter for the phone booth. Arcade games are fun, but they eat quarters.
  • If you run out of quarters at the phone exchange, every room has more - and they come back each time you dial.
  • Robots that chase you are slower than you are. Lead them around, then zap them.
  • In the Cloud Lane, watch the horizon: everything starts as a dot there. Pick your lane early; a lane change takes a moment, and so does the lane after it.
  • When the sign gets down to 1 MI, get over to the right lane and stay there. The ramp opens at 0.
  • Look both ways on the Superhighway. Trucks are slow; the teal cars are not.
  • Laser fences stay off longer than they stay on. Wait for the click, then go.
  • Pages count across all the levels. You don't need every single one.
  • Careful with the Zapper near the cover page: a zap will burn it up! If that happens, the school keeps one spare cover beside the copier. There is only the one.
  • Friendly aliens are worth a detour when you're hurt.

About this game

In The Year 2000! was made with GAME-MAKER 2.0 by Recreational Software Designs. Design, pictures, music and robot dog: Claude, for Sandbox Software.

items.title: In The Year 2000 Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Stuck in the future? Find your question, then lay the red film over the answer. Read only the one you need: the Science Fair starts at 3:00 sharp!

hints.q: Where is the Laser-Tag Zapper?
hints.a: In your own backyard, north of the garage wall. The clicker on Grandpa's key ring opens the GATE CLICK door first.

hints.q: Where are Grandpa's keys?
hints.a: In the hedge garden at the bottom left of the neighborhood. Squeeze in through the gaps in the hedges; a robo-mower guards them. The ring opens both the garage gate and the CitiCar.

hints.q: How do I leave the neighborhood?
hints.a: In Grandpa's CitiCar, plugged in by your dome. Its door has a note on it: KEYS? Find his key ring, then walk into the door. (The corner phone booths are all out of order today. Save your quarters for later.)

hints.q: Can I zap the hoverboard kids?
hints.a: No. They zoom up and down the roads, so look both ways and cross behind them.

hints.q: How do I drive this thing?
hints.a: You don't: Grandpa's CitiCar flies itself. Left and Right (or A and D) steer it one whole lane at a time. Up and Down do nothing up here.

hints.q: The traffic keeps hitting me!
hints.a: Everything comes out of the middle of the horizon as a dot, then slides into its lane. Watch which way the dot drifts, and move as soon as you know. When two lanes are blocked, the third is clear, and often has a page in it.

hints.q: Where does it end?
hints.a: Watch the sign: SKYWAY 9 MI counts down a mile every six seconds. At 0 MI the exit ramp lights up over the RIGHT lane. Be in the right lane and the car takes the ramp by itself.

hints.q: I'm low on hit points.
hints.a: Dinner pills come down the lanes too. Steer into one for a turkey dinner.

hints.q: How do I cross fourteen lanes of traffic?
hints.a: Island by island. Wait on a deck for a gap, then dash. Gold trucks are slow, red cars are medium, and the teal cars are VERY fast.

hints.q: Where is the phone booth?
hints.a: At the far right of the last platform at the bottom, past the FAX-A-PIZZA billboard. The one next to where you start is out of order.

hints.q: What does the glass tube do?
hints.a: It whisks you along to the right in a hurry. Step off the side if you want to grab a page instead.

hints.q: How do I get the STAFF ONLY keycard?
hints.a: It's in the corner of TV-RAMA behind a laser fence. Stand next to the lasers and walk through as soon as they blink off. They stay off three times longer than they stay on.

hints.q: Where is the STAFF ONLY door?
hints.a: On the south wall of the concourse, on the right. The loading dock behind it has three more laser fences and the phone booth.

hints.q: Are the arcade games worth it?
hints.a: Arcade games give 1,000 points and pinball gives 2,500, but each one eats a quarter and then it's GAME OVER. Never spend your last quarter!

hints.q: The security robots keep catching me.
hints.a: They are slower than you are. Lead them in a loop, then turn around and zap them.

hints.q: Which number do I dial?
hints.a: Booth 3 is the shortest way: inside a TV set, then the Jurassic period, then the Moon Shuttle launch pad. Booths 1 and 2 work too, they just take the scenic route. (The teletype in the corner has been trying to tell you.)

hints.q: I'm out of quarters!
hints.a: Every room has quarters, and they come back every time you dial into it. Pick them up before you dial again.

hints.q: How do I get on the Moon Shuttle?
hints.a: Walk up the boarding ramp right under the rocket. It's chained off while the countdown runs (6, 5, 4...): wait for its board to say GO. The booth on the launch pad only takes you back to the hall.

hints.q: I'm hurt. Is there help?
hints.a: Booth 1 goes to Grandma's condo in Florida. She gives a big hug that heals you.

hints.q: Where is the Moon Pass?
hints.a: At the top left of the Moon, west of the big dome. Hop up meteor alley to get it.

hints.q: How do I dodge the meteors?
hints.a: They fall at a slant from the sky along the top edge. Watch where they land, then hop through behind them.

hints.q: Where is Moon School?
hints.a: The base at the top right. Walk into the MOON PASS airlock with the pass, and the door to the Science Fair is inside.

hints.q: How do I catch Sparky?
hints.a: Zap him three times. Each zap changes his game: he roams, then plays keep-away (corner him), then gets the zoomies. Then he gets dizzy and drops the cover page.

hints.q: The cover page vanished!
hints.a: You zapped it. A zap burns the cover page up, so stop firing once Sparky drops it. The school keeps one spare cover, on the floor right beside the copier at the bottom of the gym: walk into it. There is only the one.

hints.q: What do I do at the judges' table?
hints.a: Walk into the table with 20 pages to turn them in, then walk into the COVER table behind it with the cover page. Then step up to the podium!

hints.q: The volcano projects keep erupting.
hints.a: The lava blobs wander slowly. Keep moving, and grab a food pill if you get singed.

hints.q: What's in the closet next to the launch pad?
hints.a: Some say the felt-maker left something behind. In the future not every brick is a brick.

hints.q: The closet has no door!
hints.a: It doesn't need one. Look along the Moon Shuttle pad's right wall for a brick with teal light glowing through its mortar.

hints.q: Beam me the blueprints.
hints.a: On the Moon Shuttle pad, get into the row of the boarding ramp, on the ramp's right side (don't step on the ramp itself, or you're off to the Moon). Walk right into the glowing brick: you walk straight through it. Press G to pick up the felt egg, then walk on into the rocket hatch at the far end.

items.title: The Hover Heights Herald
items.headline: IT'S THE YEAR 2000!
items.deck: Cars fly, robots mow, dinner fits in a pill; local robot dog eats science report

photo.caption: The Dynamo family dome on Dome Circle. Robots mowed this lawn.

columns: HOVER HEIGHTS - The new millennium arrived right on time last night, and so did everything else. Flying cars filled the Information Superhighway by breakfast. Robo-mowers trimmed every lawn in neat little squares.

Dinner, as everybody always said it would, now comes in a pill. "It tastes just like turkey," said one diner. "With stuffing."

The aliens next door report that they are having a lovely time and would like a hug.

One family was not celebrating. Sparky 3000, a robot dog, reportedly ate a twenty-page science report titled The Pocket Telephone. "A telephone in your POCKET?" laughed one neighbor. "What'll they think of next?"
briefs: Y2K BUG A NO-SHOW
Computers everywhere woke up fine. The only bug in Hover Heights was a robot dog.
TELEPORT RATES
Still 25 cents a call. Booth 4 at the exchange is out of order again.
WEATHER ON THE MOON
Sunny. Meteor showers this afternoon. Bring a helmet.

items.title: The wrong-number die (fold your own)
items.note: A square of paper that blows up into a die
items.heading: The Wrong-Number Die
items.intro: Cut out the square, fold it and blow it up into a six-sided die for choosing which booth to dial in the Exchange. Nothing about it is right: its faces are 1, 2, 3, a 4 that is out of order, a 7 (there is no booth 7) and a 0, which is the hole you blow in. Opposite faces add up to 4, 6 and 7. Roll it, then dial whatever it says.
items.foot: If you roll the 4, the booth is out of order. Roll again.

items.note: Dex's science fair report: the pages Sparky ate (and a few teeth marks)

news.head: Our second game: In The Year 2000!
news.html: Sandbox Software is four months old, and its second game is in your hands. In In The Year 2000! you are Dex Dynamo, age 11, and your robot dog Sparky 3000 just ate your science report. Find 20 pages across six levels of the future, from the dome homes of Hover Heights to the Moon, and get them to the Science Fair by 3:00. Bring a quarter: every phone booth is a Teleport-A-Phone.

news.head: What will the year 2000 be like?
news.html: We asked our classmates what they expect in seven short years. The top answers: flying cars (41 votes), robot dogs (29), dinner in a pill (17), and a telephone small enough to fit in your pocket (2 votes, and one of those was a joke). Our programmer is betting on the pocket telephone. Our mail room is still betting on the mail.

news.head: Sparky says thanks
news.html: Register In The Year 2000! for $12 and you get the next Sandbox Software game on a 3 1/2" disk, a printed manual and a sticker for your computer. Sparky promises not to eat any of it.

news.head: Since last issue: Snowbound, rough edges and all
news.html: Snowbound got our roughest reviews and our warmest letters. Yes, it’s the simplest game we’ll ever make; it’s also the truest. Readers from all over Mineral County wrote to say we got the sled run on Jamie Street just right. The most-asked question: does the arcade eat all your dollars? Only if you let it. Count the can (F2) before you head for the register.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Homework comes first
news.html: The founder is a junior at Frankfort High, so Sandbox Software keeps strict hours: after homework, before bed, and all day Saturday. The office is still a desk, the family 286 and a stack of graph paper. The snow shovel has moved to the porch. It may be needed again.

news.head: In the workshop: A puzzle made of pure Game-Maker
news.html: The founder's notebook is already full. First on the list is a puzzle game where electricity is made of ordinary Game-Maker blocks and monsters: switches, fuses, and a little robot who must never touch a live wire. Its working title is Ohm Sweet Ohm, and we apologize for it now. It won’t be quick: there’s homework first, and a diploma after that.

news.head: Letters: "Did you make it to the mall?"
news.html:
"In Snowbound, did the real founder make it to the register in time?" - A reader in West Virginia

The Scoop replies: Look at the name on this newsletter. Then look at the box your game came in.
